item.title: Como os houthis estão ajudando o Irã a transformar a Arábia Saudita em um ponto de pressão
item.description: Os ataques dos houthis à Arábia Saudita envolvem mais do que o Iêmen.
item.dc:creator: Samia Nakhoul
item.content:encoded: Os ataques dos houthis à Arábia Saudita envolvem mais do que o Iêmen. Ao atacar infraestruturas e atrapalhar eventos de investimento essenciais para as ambições econômicas da Arábia Saudita, eles pretendem pressionar o príncipe herdeiro saudita Mohammed bin Salman a atender às exigências dos houthis no Iêmen e a persuadir o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, a flexibilizar o bloqueio norte-americano que sufoca a economia do Irã, segundo fontes sauditas, iranianas e regionais. A campanha reflete uma avaliação do Irã e dos houthis de que a prosperidade da Arábia Saudita, suas ambições de investimento e sua exposição a perturbações a tornam um ponto de pressão vulnerável em um confronto que se estende do Estreito de Ormuz, na foz do Golfo, até Bab el-Mandeb, no Mar Vermelho. O Irã, sob crescente pressão econômica e militar após a guerra iniciada pelos EUA e por Israel em 28 de fevereiro, busca aumentar o custo da estratégia de Washington ao atacar seus parceiros regionais, afirmou Michael Knights, da consultoria estratégica Horizon Engage. “Os iranianos estão em uma situação de estrangulamento”, disse ele. Incapazes de forçar Washington a mudar de rumo diretamente, Teerã e os houthis estão “atacando a Arábia Saudita, estão atacando o ponto fraco”, acrescentou ele, explorando a vulnerabilidade econômica do reino e seu desejo de estabilidade. Os houthis têm interesse direto em amenizar o bloqueio dos EUA ao Irã, seu principal apoiador regional. Uma redução da pressão sobre Teerã provavelmente fortaleceria sua capacidade de manter o apoio político, financeiro e militar, bem como o fluxo de armas e dinheiro dos quais, segundo os EUA, o movimento depende. Mas os houthis também têm suas próprias exigências, afirmaram duas fontes sauditas e três fontes regionais familiarizadas com o pensamento saudita: o fim das operações militares sauditas e das restrições aos portos e aeroportos iemenitas, voos regulares para o Irã, restabelecimento do pagamento de salários, indenização de guerra e o fim do apoio de Riad ao governo reconhecido do Iêmen. Suas condições consolidariam o domínio houthi sobre grande parte do Iêmen. Uma autoridade sênior iraniana afirmou que os ataques houthis fazem parte de uma estratégia mais ampla do Irã e de seus aliados para reestruturar o equilíbrio de poder regional, tendo como alvo a infraestrutura energética e as principais rotas marítimas. Ele disse que Riad não pode contar com a proteção dos EUA e precisa, em vez disso, buscar negociações, acrescentando que os ataques houthis continuariam a menos que as restrições sauditas fossem suspensas. A estratégia, no entanto, coloca Mohammed bin Salman diante de um dilema, afirmam fontes familiarizadas com o pensamento saudita. A escalada arrisca uma guerra mais ampla que poderia minar sua agenda de transformação, mas as concessões correm o risco de fortalecer um movimento que há anos desafia o poder saudita. E quanto mais o conflito se prolongar, maior será a ameaça à segurança saudita, à confiança dos investidores e à Visão 2030. A assessoria de imprensa do governo saudita e o Ministério das Relações Exteriores do Irã não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentário. O porta-voz dos houthis, Mohammed Abdulsalam, negou que o grupo estivesse agindo a mando do Irã, afirmando que suas demandas se concentravam em questões humanitárias de longa data relacionadas à Arábia Saudita e incluíam o levantamento das restrições aos portos e aeroportos iemenitas, a flexibilização das restrições econômicas e o pagamento dos salários dos funcionários públicos com recursos próprios do Iêmen. “Nossas demandas humanitárias não têm nada a ver com o Irã nem com ninguém mais”, disse ele. A Arábia Saudita enfrentou uma onda crescente de ataques houthis na última semana, incluindo ataques mortais ao Aeroporto Internacional Rei Khalid, em Riad, e um ataque à Saudi Aramco, a maior exportadora de petróleo do mundo e espinha dorsal da economia, que provocou um incêndio que se espalhou por vários andares. Os ataques interromperam a principal conferência de petróleo de Riad, levando altos executivos do setor a cancelarem sua participação e forçando os organizadores a oferecer participação remota na Future Investment Initiative (FII), um fórum global anual de investimentos. Os houthis têm um histórico de ataques no interior do reino, inclusive em 2019, quando ataques às instalações da Aramco interromperam temporariamente cerca de 5% do abastecimento global de petróleo. Isso ocorreu depois que Riad interveio no Iêmen em 2015, após a tomada da capital, Sanaa, pelos houthis. A guerra se transformou em um impasse sangrento antes do cessar-fogo de 2022. No entanto, os líderes sauditas agora veem a pressão militar como sua única opção viável, disse Abdulaziz Sager, presidente do Gulf Research Center, com sede na Arábia Saudita. “Eles chegaram a um ponto em que NÃO há mais negociações”, afirmou ele. “Não têm outra escolha a não ser a ação militar.” Os houthis cada vez mais se veem negociando a partir de uma posição de força, buscando o reconhecimento de sua autoridade em Sanaa e uma flexibilização das restrições impostas ao Iêmen, disse Fawaz Gerges, analista do Oriente Médio da London School of Economics. “O que os houthis estão exigindo agora é uma paz de vencedores”, afirmou. Os Estados Unidos têm demonstrado pouca disposição para outra campanha prolongada contra os houthis desde que os bombardearam no ano passado devido a ataques à navegação no Mar Vermelho e, em seguida, concordaram com um cessar-fogo, disseram fontes familiarizadas com a posição saudita. A relutância de Washington deixa Riad diante de um conflito no qual a pressão militar por si só pode não levar a um resultado decisivo. SAUDITAS TÊM MAIS A PERDER No início da campanha houthi, Mohammed bin Salman pediu ajuda a Trump para combater os houthis, mas Trump não concordou com ataques dos EUA, disseram fontes à Reuters no mês passado. Em vez disso, Washington ofereceu assistência na identificação de alvos e compartilhamento de inteligência. Trump afirmou posteriormente que estava considerando uma possível ação contra os houthis, embora parecesse adiar qualquer resposta até depois das eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA. O Departamento de Estado dos EUA se referiu a declarações anteriores de Trump e do secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio, que condenaram os ataques houthis à Arábia Saudita. A Casa Branca não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário. Com drones e mísseis expondo vulnerabilidades nas defesas sauditas, analistas alertam que o conflito corre o risco de se tornar uma guerra de desgaste, na qual os houthis acreditam que o tempo e a geografia lhes são favoráveis. O ex-negociador norte-americano Aaron David Miller disse que a vantagem do grupo reside não apenas em sua posição próxima ao estreito de Bab el-Mandeb, mas também na assimetria do que está em jogo. “A infraestrutura saudita é muito mais valiosa do que a infraestrutura houthi”, disse ele. “Eles têm muito menos a perder do que os sauditas.” O analista do Iêmen Farea al-Muslimi disse que a campanha dos houthis contra Riad é uma tentativa de afirmar a primazia regional, arriscando um conflito muito mais amplo em toda a Península Arábica. No cerne da crise, diz ele, está o desmoronamento de um roteiro de paz de 2023 apoiado pela Arábia Saudita, que oferecia aos houthis um caminho para a legitimidade política e financiamento para a reconstrução. De acordo com o roteiro, Riad deveria ajudar a financiar os salários do setor público e a reconstrução. O conflito no Mar Vermelho descarrilou esse processo, à medida que os houthis aprofundam sua aliança com o Irã. “Estamos caminhando para o pior desfecho imaginável”, disse al-Muslimi. “Uma guerra pior do que a de 2015. Desta vez, será mais sangrenta, e a Arábia Saudita entrará nela com menos aliados.” Ele afirmou que nenhuma campanha bem-sucedida contra os houthis seria possível sem a unidade do Golfo Pérsico, principalmente entre a Arábia Saudita e os Emirados Árabes Unidos. “Os houthis não são uma ameaça apenas para a Arábia Saudita”, disse ele. “Eles ameaçam todo o Golfo e a região como um todo. Esta não é simplesmente uma guerra saudita. É uma guerra do Golfo.”

item.title: Reportagem sobre venda de pele de frango foi feita no governo Bolsonaro
item.description: Uma reportagem sobre a venda de pele de frango em supermercados não foi feita durante o governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, como indicam publicações nas redes sociais, mas em 2022, na gestão do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Uma reportagem sobre a venda de pele de frango em supermercados não foi feita durante o governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, como indicam publicações nas redes sociais, mas em 2022, na gestão do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro. “Crise: população sem dinheiro, supermercados colocam à venda o quilo de pele de frango por R$3”, dizem postagens no Facebook, no Instagram e no Threads com uma foto de Lula. O conteúdo reproduz uma reportagem exibida pelo programa Balanço Geral, da TV Record, em 17 de junho de 2022. “Com a crise econômica, tem comércio vendendo pele de frango em São Paulo. O produto, que antes era jogado no lixo, foi parar nas prateleiras por R$2,99”, noticia a matéria. Naquele mês, a inflação dos alimentos registrou alta de 0,8%, segundo o Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE). Já em junho de 2026, houve queda de 0,24%. Segundo um relatório da Organização das Nações Unidas para a Alimentação e a Agricultura (FAO, na sigla em inglês) publicado em julho, o percentual de insegurança alimentar severa no Brasil caiu de 6,6% no triênio 2021-2023 para 0,6% entre 2023-2025. VEREDICTO Enganoso. A reportagem sobre venda de pele de frango foi feita durante o governo Bolsonaro, não no de Lula. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. item.title: Why CoreWeave's troubles are rattling the AI boom
item.description: CoreWeave's mounting debt is raising fresh concerns about the AI boom, as investors question whether demand can justify the billions being borrowed to build data centres.
item.dc:creator: Anhata Rooprai, Aditya Soni
item.content:encoded: CoreWeave's (CRWV.O) mounting debt is raising fresh concerns about the AI boom, as investors question whether demand can justify the billions being borrowed to build data centres. Shares and bonds of the Nvidia-backed (NVDA.O) company [USN:L4N46112V TEXT:"have tumbled"] despite its CEO's assurances of a strong contract backlog, fueling a broader selloff in technology stocks. Here is why investors are worried and what its troubles could mean for the industry. WHAT DOES COREWEAVE DO? CoreWeave rents out computing power from Nvidia processors to companies developing and running AI, including Microsoft (MSFT.O) and OpenAI. It is one of the leading "neocloud" providers, a group of newer cloud companies that are growing rapidly to meet demand for scarce and expensive AI chips. These neocloud companies give customers access to computing power without requiring them to build their own data centers. However, supplying such capacity requires heavy upfront investment in chips and infrastructure, often financed with debt. WHAT IS ITS FINANCIAL SITUATION? The company, which has never turned a profit, has about $50 billion in debt, according to data compiled by LSEG. It raised its annual capital spending forecast by $4 billion in August [USN:L4N4481ER TEXT:"to between $35 billion and $39 billion"]. Analysts expect revenue of nearly $13 billion this year and a loss of $2.13 billion. The yields on its bonds due in 2031, which are rated junk, have spiked to about 16%, while the cost of insuring its debt against default has climbed to about 1,000 basis points, reflecting growing concern among creditors. CEO Mike Intrator told employees in an internal memo seen by Reuters that its deal backlog more than covers its debt obligations. The company had a $104.2 billion revenue backlog at the end of the second quarter, followed by [USN:L6N4590TM TEXT:"more than $25 billion"] in new commitments early in the third quarter. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has also downplayed the concerns, saying CoreWeave's financial strength is improving and he sees no need to backstop it. The chip giant has agreed to buy unsold CoreWeave capacity through April 2032. WHY IT COULD BE A CANARY IN THE COAL MINE CoreWeave's business depends on two things: demand for AI computing and lenders' willingness to finance the infrastructure supplying it. But a selloff in its shares suggests a lack of confidence among investors in the latter, even as the company cites strong demand. The concern is not that AI demand will collapse, but that higher borrowing costs could make the business harder to sustain if demand were to weaken sharply. "It looks more like investors questioning how the build-out is being funded than a sudden collapse in appetite for AI computing," said Axel Rudolph, chief technical analyst at IG Group. "CoreWeave is quickly becoming the AI trade's canary in the coal mine," said Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB. WHY ARE MARKETS FRETTING? Investors are questioning whether AI revenue can grow fast enough to cover the cost of building and financing the infrastructure. CoreWeave has to spend heavily upfront before it can collect the revenue from its contracts. Higher interest rates could drive up financing costs and further squeeze returns. The hardware itself poses another risk. Chips lose value as newer generations arrive, pushing providers to spend even more to replace them. The concerns, however, go beyond CoreWeave. US technology giants are expected to spend more than $700 billion on AI infrastructure this year. THE DOWNSIDE SCENARIO One potential consequence would be a broader financing squeeze, with lenders demanding higher returns or becoming less willing to fund other AI projects. That could force providers to scale back expansion, curbing equipment purchases and affecting the computing capacity customers expect. A setback could also deepen doubts that the AI investment frenzy is outpacing returns, piling further pressure on technology stocks. The impact of the fallout would depend on how the business is reorganized, and CoreWeave's ties to major technology companies do not, by themselves, mean its failure would trigger a wider financial crisis. WHO ELSE BEARS THE RISK? Gartner estimates about 80% of neoclouds could shut down by 2030, warning that expected AI revenue will not support profitable returns on all planned infrastructure spending. Neocloud rivals Nebius (NBIS.O) , Applied Digital (APLD.O) and Iren (IREN.O) have fallen in the recent selloff. The cost of default protection has risen for SoftBank (9984.T) , which is betting heavily on OpenAI. Meanwhile, spreads for Amazon (AMZN.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Meta (META.O) and Nvidia have also reached records, although they have risen much more slowly than CoreWeave's. However, these companies also have larger cash flows and stronger balance sheets.

item.title: Nineteen hurt after minibus hits train at French channel tunnel terminal
item.description: At least 19 people were injured on Thursday evening after a minibus collided with a train at a loading platform for the Channel Tunnel in northern France, the local prefect's office said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 19 people were injured on Thursday evening after a minibus collided with a train at a loading platform for the Channel Tunnel in northern France, the local prefect's office said. None of the injuries were life-threatening, the prefecture said in a statement, adding that ambulances, a helicopter and police were at the scene. The accident involved a minibus carrying truck drivers who were preparing to board the Le Shuttle service on the loading platform at the Eurotunnel site, the prefecture said in a later statement. The minibus crashed into a train about to leave, it said.

item.title: É falso que Cury “voltou atrás” sobre Flávio e decidiu apoiar Lula
item.description: É falso que Augusto Cury (Avante) tenha decidido apoiar Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no segundo turno das eleições presidenciais, como alegam posts nas redes sociais. A equipe de Cury desmentiu a afirmação.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: É falso que Augusto Cury (Avante) tenha decidido apoiar Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no segundo turno das eleições presidenciais, como alegam posts nas redes sociais. A equipe de Cury desmentiu a afirmação. Estes são os principais detalhes: Postagens no Facebook e no Threads espalham uma imagem com o texto “Augusto Cury volta atrás e decide apoiar Lula junto com Renan”. A assessoria de imprensa de Cury disse que o conteúdo é “fake” e que ele apoia Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Em 8 de outubro, Cury publicou um vídeo em suas redes sociais declarando apoio a Flávio no segundo turno. O vídeo a favor de Flávio seguia no ar nesta quinta-feira. Não há registros de declarações públicas indicando uma mudança de posição de Cury. Também citado nos posts checados, o ex-candidato a presidente Renan Santos (Missão) não declarou apoio a Lula ou Flávio. Procurada, a assessoria de Renan disse que o político “já se posicionou afirmando neutralidade no segundo turno.” Veredicto: Falso. A equipe de Cury negou que ele tenha retirado o apoio a Flávio e decidido endossar Lula no segundo turno. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. item.title: Comcast owes $213 million in video-streaming patent dispute, US jury says
item.description: A jury in Tampa, Florida, found on Thursday that Comcast owes digital television provider WhereverTV $213 million in damages for infringing a patent related to streaming video.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: A jury in Tampa, Florida, found on Thursday that Comcast (CMCSA.O) owes digital television provider WhereverTV $213 million in damages for infringing a patent related to streaming video. The jury agreed with Fort Myers-based WhereverTV that Comcast's X1 set-top boxes violate its patent rights in technology for integrating cable channels with streaming services, according to a copy of the verdict provided by WhereverTV's attorneys A spokesperson and attorneys for Comcast did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the verdict WhereverTV's founder Mark Cavicchia invented the patented technology covering "novel systems for receiving, accessing, managing, and viewing digital content from different sources," the company said in a court filing The lawsuit, filed in 2018, said that Comcast integrated the technology into its X1 platform around 2012 when it was "losing subscribers and market share due to so-called cord cutters" Comcast denied the allegations and argued that the patent was invalid A Florida judge ruled that Comcast did not infringe the patent during an earlier jury trial in 2023, but the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit overturned his ruling in 2025 and sent the case back for a new trial The case is WhereverTV Inc v. Comcast Corp, US District Court for the Middle District of Florida, No. 2:18-cv-00529. For WhereverTV: Adam Sanderson of Reese Marketos For Comcast: Traci McKee of Faegre Drinker Biddle & Reath

item.title: League pouring resources into flag football training, development ahead of LA28
item.description: The NFL is developing a tech platform geared toward flag football training, the league's senior vice president for global flag football Brian Flinn said on Thursday, as it continues an aggressive push into the game.
item.dc:creator: Amy Tennery
item.content:encoded: The NFL is developing a tech platform geared toward flag football training, the league's senior vice president for global flag football Brian Flinn said on Thursday, as it continues an aggressive push into the game. The platform will address the training and development gap in the sport, said Flinn, with the non-tackle form of the game seeing a surge in participation ahead of its Olympic debut at LA28. "No one's really done the work to understand how unique the discipline is and what training modules do you need to get athletes ready," said Flinn, appearing at the Columbia University Sports Management Conference. "We're working with third-party experts in that space to develop curriculum so that we can train athletes to go a little bit further. "And then on the coaching and officiating side, the reality is there's a lot of great people out there, in some cases volunteering their time. And it's not an indictment on them, but the reality is no one's invested in them to develop them to keep up with the demanding players at every level." Flag football has emerged as a key piece of the NFL's global strategy as it included a [USN:L6N41Q13I TEXT:"record nine games"] in its international schedule this season. The league is [USN:L6N44U08L TEXT:"chasing millions"] of fans outside the US, after launching its [USN:L1N2T02NX TEXT:"global markets"] programme in 2021. The sport is widely perceived as having a lower barrier to entry for newcomers with less risk of injuries commonly seen in the bone-crunching tackle sport, and the NFL views flag as a way of getting [USN:L1N3MC10A TEXT:"more women"] and girls into its orbit. The NFL earlier this year announced plans to launch a professional flag football league for men and women. "The reality is we need to make more investment in player health and safety," said Flinn. "My expectations in the next three or four months, we'll have a tech platform out there that is training people at scale."

item.title: Report: Thomas Pieters not on board for LIV Golf 2.0
item.description: Thomas Pieters will not sign up for LIV Golf 2.0 and plans to play on the DP World Tour next year, he confirmed to Flushing It Golf.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thomas Pieters will not sign up for LIV Golf 2.0 and plans to play on the DP World Tour next year, he confirmed to Flushing It Golf. The 34-year-old Belgian was a member of captain Dustin Johnson's 4 Aces team for the past two seasons in LIV Golf. Pieters is a six-time winner on the DP World Tour, most recently at the Abu Dhabi HSBC Championship in January 2022. He joined LIV Golf in 2023 and reportedly earned more than $25 million in prize money. Pieters competed on the 2016 European Ryder Cup team, posting a 4-1-0 record in a 17-11 loss to the United States at Hazeltine. He joins other notable names who are not returning to LIV Golf as it attempts to restructure without financing from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. Spanish superstar and three-time LIV Golf individual season champion Jon Rahm tops that list, which also includes Sergio Garcia, Abraham Ancer, David Puig and Adrian Meronk. --Field Level Media

item.title: Amar'e Stoudemire goes from Miami Heat to Miami police officer
item.description: Amar'e Stoudemire has traded in his jersey and shorts for a dress uniform and a badge.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Amar'e Stoudemire has traded in his jersey and shorts for a dress uniform and a badge. Now 43, the former All-NBA player and recent enshrinee to the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame, graduated from the Miami Dade College School of Justice's Basic Law Enforcement Academy on Thursday. He will move into a position as an officer with the county's school police department. On its X account, the college posted photos of the smiling 6-foot-10 Stoudemire with his classmates and teachers. A statement from Miami Dade College explained Stoudemire's motivation. "For Amar'e, this is more than a second career," the school announced in a post on X. "Becoming a police officer was a childhood dream, inspired in part by family members who served in law enforcement. Now, he will begin a new chapter as a police officer with the Miami Dade Schools Police Department, giving back to our community and serving as a positive influence for the next generation." Born in Florida, Stoudemire went straight from high school to the NBA, selected with the ninth overall pick in 2002 by the Phoenix Suns. He was named NBA Rookie of the Year in 2003 and was a six-time All-Star. He played primarily for the Suns and New York Knicks, and briefly, at the end of his career, for the Dallas Mavericks and Heat. In his final NBA season, 2015-16, he appeared in 52 games for Miami. The following season, he played for a pro team in Israel. Stoudemire averaged 18.9 points and 7.8 rebounds over his 846 regular-season games (696 starts). --Field Level Media

item.title: Diesel's surge is starting to push other prices around. Here's how
item.description: The skyrocketing price of diesel is plain for Americans to see anytime they fuel up their cars, SUVs and pickup trucks, though only a fraction of US drivers own a diesel-powered vehicle so they may think they are dodging that massive sticker shock.
item.dc:creator: Dan Burns
item.content:encoded: The skyrocketing price of diesel is plain for Americans to see anytime they fuel up their cars, SUVs and pickup trucks, though only a fraction of US drivers own a diesel-powered vehicle so they may think they are dodging that massive sticker shock. Think again. Wholesale inflation data from the Labor Department on Thursday showed US producer prices climbed far more than expected in September — auguring more stiff inflation at the consumer level in the weeks and months ahead as those costs get passed along. Evidence of the impact of high energy prices, record-high diesel prices in particular, was all over that 34-page readout. Why? Because, as Oxford Economics wrote recently: "Diesel is the workhorse fuel of the economy." Here are some of the ways diesel is driving up producer inflation and how that threatens to drive up a range of consumer costs further soon. GETTING IT TO YOUR DOOR If you own it, eat it or drink it, a truck was involved somewhere along the way in bringing it — either to where you picked it up or to your house. The vast majority of those vehicles in the US goods transportation fleet run on diesel. So when diesel prices more than double as they have over the last year, the cost of moving all that stuff around goes up and soon those shippers begin demanding higher prices for that service. In September, the Producer Price Index's gauge of the cost for truck transportation of freight was up by 19% year over year, the most in just over four years. What's more, those freight transportation costs are responding much faster to the surge in diesel prices than they did to the price surge following the COVID-19 pandemic. That's because the overall economy is in a much better position now than it was then, with the US jobless rate at a still historically low 4.2% supporting robust demand. Also the absolute price of the fuel is more than twice what it was as the pandemic recovery began. FARM TO TABLE Diesel is critical to farming, powering the tractors and harvesting equipment involved in producing food and again in fueling the trucks that take it to grocery stores and restaurants. While end-user consumer food cost increases in both PPI and the Consumer Price Index in September were pretty benign, costs further back in the food supply chain are rising fast. The average of food inputs at stages one and two of what PPI calls "intermediate demand" - which reflect producers' own energy costs and the energy costs embedded in producing key things farmers use like fertilizers and other agricultural chemicals — was up 15.6% from a year earlier in September, again by the most in about four years. Prices for energy-sensitive feed products like corn, hay and hayseeds and oilseeds all shot up by more than 25% year over year. If history is any guide, households should brace for yet higher grocery store prices in the months ahead. "We expect a pickup in food inflation later this year," Oxford's senior US economist Matthew Martin said after the PPI report. ENERGY & CPI The US economy is far less energy-intensive than it was during the oil shocks of the 1970s, but it is still has an impact on prices overall — and more so the longer they stay high. PPI categories like materials for manufacturing — inputs that are themselves absorbing higher diesel costs to produce and deliver — are rising at double-digit annual rates. Producers must take the hit to their margins or pass the costs along. CHRISTMAS IS COMING The diesel surge threatens to make the coming holiday season more expensive — and is already a factor in one of the season's biggest staples: Toys. Prices for toys — exposed to higher shipping costs among other things — rose in September by the most ever month over month.

item.title: Al Pacino recibirá el premio a la trayectoria de la Asociación de Actores
item.description: El célebre actor Al Pacino recibirá el año que viene un premio a su trayectoria por los logros de su vida profesional y su labor humanitaria, anunció este jueves el sindicato de actores SAG-AFTRA.
item.dc:creator: Danielle Broadway
item.content:encoded: El célebre actor Al Pacino recibirá el año que viene un premio a su trayectoria por los logros de su vida profesional y su labor humanitaria, anunció este jueves el sindicato de actores SAG-AFTRA. El actor estadounidense, conocido sobre todo por interpretar a Michael Corleone en la saga de "El padrino", es el sexagésimo segundo galardonado con el Premio SAG-AFTRA a toda una vida de logros. El sindicato le entregará el premio en Los Ángeles, durante la trigésimo tercera edición de los Actor Awards, el 28 de febrero de 2027, en el marco de una ceremonia que transmitirá en directo Netflix. (NFLX.O) El reconocimiento a Pacino llega tras una carrera que abarca más de seis décadas en el cine, la televisión y el teatro. El actor es conocido por numerosos personajes memorables, entre ellos el policía Frank Serpico en "Serpico" (1973), el mafioso de Miami Tony Montana en "Caracortada" (1983) y, más recientemente, el agente de Hollywood Marvin Schwarz en "Érase una vez en Hollywood", la película de Quentin Tarantino de 2019. El premio se entrega anualmente a quien encarne los "mejores ideales de la profesión de actor", según el sindicato. "Me he hecho preguntas y he vagado durante la mayor parte de mi vida, pero siempre me he sentido como en casa con un guión y mis compañeros de reparto", dijo Pacino en un comunicado del sindicato de actores. "El trabajo y los actores con los que he compartido este camino han sido una de las mayores alegrías de mi vida. Es un honor que SAG-AFTRA reconozca esta trayectoria", añadió. Pacino ganó el Óscar al mejor actor por su interpretación del teniente coronel Frank Slade en la película de 1992 "Perfume de mujer", y también ha obtenido múltiples premios Emmy, Tony y Globos de Oro. "Al igual que tantos actores, he pasado mi vida admirando y apreciando esa fuerza de la naturaleza que es Al Pacino. Cuando le ves actuar, estás presenciando a un alumno y a un maestro", añadió el presidente de SAG-AFTRA, Sean Astin, en el comunicado. El actor, de 86 años, nació en Nueva York con el nombre de Alfredo James Pacino. Pasó toda la década de los sesenta luchando por encontrar un trabajo estable antes de que, finalmente, su carrera cinematográfica despegó con "El padrino", de 1972. SAG-AFTRA representa a aproximadamente 160.000 actores, locutores, periodistas de televisión, bailarines, DJ, redactores de noticias, editores de noticias, presentadores de programas, titiriteros, artistas discográficos, cantantes, especialistas, locutores, 'influencers' y otros profesionales del entretenimiento y los medios de comunicación.

item.title: Indian mutual funds stop bulk subscriptions to gold ETFs ahead of festive season
item.description: Several large Indian mutual funds issued public notices late on Thursday suspending bulk subscriptions to gold exchange-traded funds, just ahead of the festive season when investor demand typically rises.
item.dc:creator: Ira Dugal, Rajendra Jadhav
item.content:encoded: Several large Indian mutual funds issued public notices late on Thursday suspending bulk subscriptions to gold exchange-traded funds, just ahead of the festive season when investor demand typically rises. The notices from the fund houses, including Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, UTI Mutual Fund and HDFC Mutual Fund, did not cite a reason for the move. There is no restriction on redemptions from these funds. The decision was taken following a nudge from the Securities and Exchange Board of India, according to a mutual fund executive familiar with the discussions. Two bullion industry officials confirmed the halt had followed discussions with the market regulator. The sources declined to be identified as they are not permitted to comment on discussions with the regulator. A spokesperson for SEBI did not respond to a Reuters request for comment outside business hours. The [USN:L1N45X01Q TEXT:"Indian rupee has been under pressure this year"] due to a surge in global oil prices, which have inflated the country's import bill, and heavy selling by foreign investors in Indian equities. Strong demand for gold has further weighed on the currency, prompting the government to raise import duties on gold and silver earlier this year. India, the world's largest consumer of silver and second-largest consumer of gold, relies on imports to meet most of its demand, a dependence that can sometimes widen its trade deficit. Gold imports fell to $1.8 billion in September, from $2.3 billion in August. However, Indians will celebrate Dussehra in October and Diwali in early November, when buying gold is considered auspicious. Inflows into gold and silver ETFs surged during last year's festive season as investors turned to precious metals amid lackluster stock market returns. The move is surprising, as gold and silver imports have fallen sharply over the past two months from a year earlier and have not contributed to the trade deficit, said a dealer at a private bank that supplies bullion to ETFs. "It looks more like a precautionary measure to avoid a surge in imports in October," the dealer said.

item.title: Masiva marcha universitaria contra Milei concluye con incidentes en Argentina
item.description: Una multitudinaria protesta de argentinos contra el ajuste del presidente ultraliberal Javier Milei sobre la educación concluyó el jueves con incidentes con la policía frente al Congreso de la Nación.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Una multitudinaria protesta de argentinos contra el ajuste del presidente ultraliberal Javier Milei sobre la educación concluyó el jueves con incidentes con la policía frente al Congreso de la Nación. Los manifestantes, mayormente estudiantes, docentes y ciudadanos independientes, reclamaban al presidente el cumplimiento de una ley dictada por el Congreso para revertir la reducción del presupuesto universitario, que el Gobierno ha desoído pese a diversos fallos judiciales en su contra. La protesta refleja el profundo malestar de gran parte de la clase media argentina con el ajuste que el mandatario aplicó sobre la economía -en particular sobre sectores sensibles como educación y salud- para reducir la inflación. Ese disgusto se observa en la baja popularidad de Milei que muestra la mayoría de las encuestas de opinión. Autoridades de la Universidad de Buenos Aires (UBA), que cuenta con más de 300.000 estudiantes y varios premios Nobel a lo largo de su historia, estimaron que su personal perdió cerca del 30% de su salario bajo la gestión de la derecha radical. "No normalicemos el incumplimiento de la ley. Las leyes se cumplen. Siempre", publicó en redes sociales la UBA para convocar a la protesta que se desarrollaba frente al Congreso de la Nación. Con inmensas banderas y pancartas a favor de la educación pública, la multitudinaria convocatoria mantuvo paralizado el centro de la ciudad. Pero antes del acto principal hubo enfrentamientos entre la policía y un grupo minoritario situado entre los manifestantes, frente al Congreso, en Buenos Aires, que acabó con heridos y aceleró el fin de la protesta. "Nuestro reclamo es por el financiamiento, por el presupuesto universitario que hace más de 350 días que el Gobierno no cumple. Vamos a seguir luchando por la universidad pública, gratuita y de calidad", dijo a Reuters Juan Sgró, profesor de la Facultad de Artes de la Universidad Nacional de Córdoba. La protesta se replicó en otras importantes ciudades del país como Rosario y Córdoba.

item.title: Martinez apologises for Man United criticism after Carrick talks
item.description: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez apologised on Thursday for criticising the club's hierarchy following their Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid, after holding talks with manager Michael Carrick and senior officials.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez apologised on Thursday for criticising the club's hierarchy following their Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid, after holding talks with manager Michael Carrick and senior officials. Martinez met with Carrick and club executives after training, two days after saying the club needed greater investment to help the team compete at the highest level following Tuesday's 2-0 loss. "Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager," Martinez said in an Instagram post, in his second statement since the interview. "It was a very positive conversation where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game." A club source said that any internal disciplinary action would remain private, adding that it had been Martinez's decision to apologise publicly and that all parties considered the matter closed. Martinez acknowledged that his frustration following the defeat had got the better of him and apologised for choosing the wrong moment to air his feelings. "Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity," he said. "The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise." The Argentina international had singled out director of football Jason Wilcox in the post-game interview, saying United needed more signings to compete with their rivals and build a squad capable of challenging in Europe. Martinez said his comments had not reflected the unity required at Old Trafford and stressed his belief that everyone at the club was working towards the same goal. "Our club is at its best when we are all united, and I recognise that my words in that moment did not come up with that," he said. "I know that every single person at Manchester United is doing everything possible to achieve our shared ambition, bringing the success that this club and its supporters deserve." Martinez finished his statement by drawing a line under the episode. "With this situation now behind us, we are fully focused on winning together." United are 13th in the Premier League after six games in their worst start in 40 years. They travel to seventh-placed Leeds United on Sunday.

item.title: Judge calls $3,000 hourly rate 'patently unreasonable' as lawyer billing soars
item.description: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com)
item.dc:creator: David Thomas, Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com ) A California federal judge approved more than $22.6 million in legal fees this week in a $68 million privacy settlement with Google over its voice-activated assistant, but criticized some of the lawyers' billing rates, including a proposed $3,000 hourly rate that the court called "patently unreasonable." US District Judge Beth Labson Freeman in San Jose refused to accept the $3,000 rate for David Scott of plaintiffs' firm Scott + Scott and reduced it to $1,600 an hour for purposes of calculating the overall class action fee award. "It is not unusual for named partners to charge more than other partners. And the court is cognizant that rates increase year to year. But not to $3,000 an hour," Freeman wrote . Still, the court granted the lawyers' request for 33% of the settlement fund and called the award reasonable and consistent with market rates. Spokespersons for Scott + Scott and the US District Court for the Northern District of California declined to comment. A $3,000 hourly rate may have struck the judge as an overreach in this case, but such figures are no longer a shock among top lawyers at major firms. Reuters has reported [USN:L6N3YQ00F TEXT:"rates as high as $4,000"] for prominent lawyers at Susman Godfrey. [USN:L6N45K07C TEXT:"Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher;"] [USN:L1N3TM04N TEXT:"Milbank"] and Quinn Emanuel are among firms with some partner rates over $3,000. "Lawyers operate in a market, and for better or worse, $3,000 per hour is now very much market rate for top tier partners at large firms," Adam Levitin, a bankruptcy law professor at Georgetown University, said in an email. Levitin and Nancy Rapoport, a fee examiner and law professor at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, said the courts regularly approve hourly fees in that range for debtors' counsel in bankruptcy matters. Law firm billing rates are typically not public, but lawyers are sometimes required to disclose them in certain cases like bankruptcies and class actions where judges must approve fees. Rapoport said that while hourly rates can attract the most attention, it's the staffing on a case that drives up the costs. "Too many people at a hearing, too many people at a meeting, or the wrong people doing the wrong kind of work. That drives up fees way more than the billable hour," she said. Freeman did not criticize the plaintiffs' lawyers' staffing in the Google privacy case, and said they achieved an "excellent" settlement. Class action plaintiffs' lawyers typically work on contingency and don't receive fees if they lose. Annual billing rate increases are [USN:L1N3UE0PZ TEXT:"key revenue and profit drivers"] for law firms. Hourly rates among large US firms grew by an average of 7% in 2025, according to a report this year by the Thomson Reuters Institute and Georgetown Law's Center on Ethics and the Legal Profession. The Thomson Reuters Institute and Reuters share the same parent company. Scott + Scott said in its July fee request that its rates are partly based on the "prevailing market rates for attorneys and law firms in California that have comparable skill, experience, and qualifications," and defended its rates as reasonable. Scott, managing partner of the 150-lawyer firm, billed about 64 hours as part of the lawsuit, records show, amounting to $194,100 in fees. Another lawyer at the firm, Daryl Scott, billed at $1,960 an hour in the lawsuit, according to billing records the firm submitted as part of its fee request. The settlement resolves claims that Google's Assistant illegally recorded and disseminated private conversations after it was triggered, and used them to send targeted advertising. Google denied wrongdoing, but settled to avoid the risk, cost and uncertainty of litigation, court papers show. A Google spokesperson said the company was pleased to resolve the case. The judge used the hourly rates submitted by the plaintiffs' lawyers as part of her review of the compensation request. She applied a $1,600 rate cap on other plaintiffs' lawyers in the case. Daryl Scott had his hourly rate lowered from $1,960. Geoffrey Horn and Vincent Briganti of Lowey Dannenberg, which also represented the plaintiffs, had initially submitted hourly rates of $1,795. Lowey attorneys declined to comment. ALSO ON BILLABLE HOURS' RADAR THIS WEEK.... --Cornell University hired US law firm King & Spalding to conduct an independent investigation into its policies and procedures following a public outcry over the Ivy League school's handling of an alleged gang rape. But the public may not see the investigation's results, education attorneys told Reuters columnist Sara [USN:L6N45V14Z TEXT:"Randazzo"], because of the risks of exposing the university to more litigation. --2025's white law graduates are securing jobs at a higher rate than their Black, Hispanic and Asian classmates, [USN:L6N46014N TEXT:"according to new figures"] released by the National Association for Law Placement. --Partners are continuing to leave traditional law firms for new startup firms that bill themselves as "AI-native," [USN:L6N46019U TEXT:"including"] the departure of a Goodwin Procter partner to lead a new US law firm associated with Zurich-founded technology company Omnilex AI.
