item.title: Italy's UniCredit wins ECB approval to control Germany's Commerzbank
item.description: UniCredit , Italy's second-largest bank, said on Thursday that the European Central Bank had authorised it to take control of Commerzbank , after a hostile takeover offer completed in July lifted its stake in the German rival to 48%.
item.dc:creator: Valentina Za
item.content:encoded: UniCredit (CRDI.MI) , Italy's second-largest bank, said on Thursday that the European Central Bank had authorised it to take control of Commerzbank (CBKG.DE) , after [USN:L8N43A0H6 TEXT:"a hostile takeover offer completed"] in July lifted its stake in the German rival to 48%. UniCredit needed ECB approval to take delivery of the Commerzbank shares tendered in the €45 billion offer and advance plans for what would be Europe's biggest cross-border banking deal since the global financial crisis. UniCredit said the ECB had authorised it to cross the 30% ownership threshold in Commerzbank and "to increase its stake further without upper limits." It added it expected to be able to take control of Commerzbank by the end of the year with around 50% of voting rights, after completing the "remaining regulatory processes and conditions" relating to its takeover bid. The Italian bank, which has operated Bavarian lender HVB in Germany since 2005, started investing in Commerzbank more than two years ago, as UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel embarked on a takeover that several of his predecessors had also studied. Despite stiff opposition from Commerzbank and criticism from the German government, UniCredit secured enough shares to control ordinary shareholder resolutions while remaining below the 50% threshold that would force it to buy out minority investors in the German lender's Polish unit mBank (MBK.WA) . Orcel has told Commerzbank to adopt the strategy he has mapped out to boost profits at [USN:L8N43P07Z TEXT:"the Frankfurt-based bank from January"], while pushing back a full merger to 2029-2030. The veteran dealmaker has held talks with [USN:L4N45L0A6 TEXT:"German government representatives who want Commerzbank"] to retain its Frankfurt headquarters, to protect jobs and to lend to German businesses. Once in possession of the shares, Orcel [USN:L4N45L0A6 TEXT:"has threatened to call"] a shareholder vote and install a new supervisory board and management at Commerzbank, without waiting for its annual general meeting next year.

item.title: FIFA to amend Article 27 of disciplinary code after Balogun case
item.description: FIFA will amend its disciplinary regulations after controversy over its decision to suspend U.S. forward Folarin Balogun’s automatic World Cup ban, the Belgian Football Association (RBFA) said on Thursday after raising the issue with soccer’s governing body.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: FIFA will amend its disciplinary regulations after controversy over its decision to suspend U.S. forward Folarin Balogun’s automatic World Cup ban, the Belgian Football Association (RBFA) said on Thursday after raising the issue with soccer’s governing body. The decision follows criticism of FIFA’s move to suspend Balogun’s automatic one-match ban for a red card, allowing the striker to play against Belgium in their last-16 clash. U.S. President Donald Trump said he had personally asked FIFA President Gianni Infantino to review the sanction, prompting questions about the independence of the disciplinary process. Following Thursday's FIFA Council meeting in Zurich, RBFA president and FIFA Council member Pascale Van Damme said the governing body would revise Article 27 of its Disciplinary Code, which allows the implementation of a disciplinary sanction to be suspended in exceptional circumstances. The proposed amendment will be submitted for approval at the next FIFA Council meeting in Doha on December 16, the Belgian federation said. "FIFA’s confirmation that Article 27 will be amended, following the request we had already submitted in July, is an important step. The proposed amendment, together with an explanation of the specific circumstances of the Balogun case, will be submitted in Doha," said Van Damme. The RBFA had sought clarification from FIFA over the circumstances surrounding the decision, saying it had not received satisfactory explanations about how Article 27 had been applied or what criteria would govern comparable cases. RBFA has also asked FIFA to provide assurances that there had been no external interference in the disciplinary proceedings, to explain the exceptional circumstances that justified the use of Article 27, and to guarantee that member associations would have the right to be heard in future disciplinary cases. According to the RBFA, FIFA responded by stressing that all decisions are taken independently by its judicial bodies and confirmed that work was already underway on amending Article 27. The Belgian federation had requested that the [USN:L4N44Z0KQ TEXT:"Balogun"] case be placed on the agenda for Thursday’s Council meeting as it sought greater transparency over the process.

item.title: Trump says he wants death penalty for anyone who kills a firefighter
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday he wants the death penalty for anyone who kills a firefighter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday he wants the death penalty for anyone who kills a firefighter. Trump, who previously has called for the death penalty for anyone found guilty of killing a police officer, made the comment during a White House Rose Garden lunch honoring firefighter organizations. Trump said he had directed the Justice Department to seek the death penalty in such cases, specifically "anybody that murders a firefighter going up a ladder."

item.title: Amazon launches two new portable AI listening devices
item.description: Amazon unveiled two new devices on Thursday for listening to and recording people's information throughout the day to offer calendar reminders and other AI-driven insights under the Bee brand it acquired last year.
item.dc:creator: Greg Bensinger
item.content:encoded: Amazon (AMZN.O) unveiled two new devices on Thursday for listening to and recording people's information throughout the day to offer calendar reminders and other AI-driven insights under the [USN:L6N3TJ0TT TEXT:"Bee brand"] it acquired last year. Frontier is a bracelet and Eclipse is a brick that resembles a portable magnetic charger. Users attach the Eclipse to their smartphones. The devices aggregate information from calendars, apps and other data throughout the day, Amazon said. The Frontier bracelet costs $75 and the Eclipse $100, Amazon said. "They listen to your whole day," said Amazon devices chief Panos Panay at the TechCrunch Disrupt conference in San Francisco. "It reminds you of the conversations you had, it reminds you of to-dos that you may have had, it tells you that you have some action items that you committed to other people." USERS CONTROL PRIVACY: AMAZON He said that because the devices are always listening when turned on, users do not have to make reminders for themselves and "can stay more present" throughout the day. The company said users control privacy by deciding when to turn it on and can delete insights or prior conversations as they see fit. Amazon does not store audio. The company faced criticism after reports in 2019 that thousands of people were listening to conversations people had with its Alexa voice assistant service. It is facing a [USN:L1N3T40PK TEXT:"class action lawsuit"] over the practice. Amazon has denied any wrongdoing. Bee will retain data for 14 days, though users can extend that by paying for a $12-per-month subscription. The devices can also connect to Alexa+, Amazon's subscription generative AI voice service. Amazon's Bee will face competition in AI wearables, notably Meta's (META.O) Muse Charm, a pendant using the company's latest agentic AI software, and its eyeglasses with cameras and other sensors. A host of startups have also developed similar devices, designed to record conversations and take action on behalf of users. In recent weeks, Amazon has announced a flurry of new gadgets, part of Panay's effort to attract buyers willing to spend more for higher quality and durability. A slate of tablets Amazon announced last week costs as much as three times more than prior versions, despite [USN:L6N45T1AE TEXT:"slowing global sales"] of the portable computers. Reuters reported earlier this year that Amazon is considering a [USN:L6N4071DB TEXT:"return to the smartphone market"] about a decade after the release of its failed Fire Phone.

item.title: Anthropic grants outside evaluator METR employee-level access in AI safety push
item.description: Anthropic has given nonprofit METR employee-level access to its systems and is in talks with others including Hugging Face, as AI companies pitch external evaluators as a way to safely advance the technology without slowing its development.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Soni
item.content:encoded: Anthropic has given nonprofit METR employee-level access to its systems and is in talks with others including Hugging Face, as AI companies pitch external evaluators as a way to safely advance the technology without slowing its development. The developer of Claude models is also working with biosecurity nonprofit SecureBio and Accenture's AI business Faculty as evaluators, it said in a blog post on Thursday. Reuters [USN:L1N45S0TG TEXT:"exclusively reported earlier this week"] that Anthropic and OpenAI had sought significant control over what outside reviewers could publish, concerned that the findings could leak trade secrets. A person familiar with the matter told Reuters that talks with Anthropic had evolved recently, with the company becoming more open in negotiations. A key sticking point between evaluators and AI labs is that information the companies might consider crucial intellectual property can also be relevant to assessing a model's risks, leading to disputes and redactions, a separate person familiar with the discussions told Reuters. Experts have also said the independence of evaluators is a concern, as Anthropic and OpenAI choose who gets to carry out the reviews. The outcome of the talks will help determine how the world scrutinizes a technology that [USN:L4N4610V0 TEXT:"some of its creators"] warn may be advancing beyond humanity's ability to manage. THE METR TIE-UP Anthropic said on Thursday six employees of METR — or Model Evaluation and Threat Research — have company hardware, office space and access to internal systems roughly equivalent to its risk assessment teams. However, customer data, legally privileged information and model architecture will remain off limits. The company said it cannot veto METR's findings on risks, incidents and practices, but can require narrowly defined redactions. METR can also publicly question those redactions without revealing the withheld information. "In line with our transparency policies, our report will openly describe the scope, access, and other limitations of our work," METR said. The nonprofit had proposed on Wednesday that developers allow private staff interviews, timely publication of assessments and transparency about access limits and redactions. Anthropic said its other evaluator partnerships are at an early stage, with more limited access and publication rights. The company is developing three tiers of access. Evaluators at the first level will conduct narrowly scoped investigations and need approval to publish. Those at the second will receive more information and can publish without approval, subject to redactions evaluators can publicly challenge. The third, used by METR, provides employee-like access with similar publication rights to the second tier. SecureBio is in the first tier and is reviewing the chemical and biological weapons chapter of Anthropic's August risk report, having published a pilot review of the previous report. Anthropic said it would consider expanding SecureBio's access and publication rights after the review. Anthropic also announced last month that it is working on a tie-up with Faculty covering model evaluations, adversarial testing and assessments of whether models behave as intended, among other areas.

item.title: Bearman ready to step up as team leader at Haas F1, says Komatsu
item.description: Ollie Bearman is ready to step up as leader on the track at Haas next season, the US-owned team's principal Ayao Komatsu said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ollie Bearman is ready to step up as leader on the track at Haas next season, the US-owned team's principal Ayao Komatsu said on Thursday. The Japanese was speaking to reporters after Haas announced [USN:L6N461143 TEXT:"Brazilian rookie Rafael Camara"] as Esteban Ocon's replacement on a multi-year deal from 2027. Frenchman Ocon, a past race winner with Renault-owned Alpine, is leaving at the end of the season and while Bearman has yet to be confirmed, the Ferrari-backed Briton looks sure to stay. "I cannot go into certain contractual details but of course I'd like to continue with Ollie," said Komatsu. "He's an incredible talent and he's shown amazing growth. This year he's shown that he's ready to be a team leader". Bearman, 21, has scored 23 of Haas's 30 points so far from 17 rounds this season. In Singapore last weekend the Briton finished sixth in the Saturday sprint race after starting 13th, on a track where overtaking is extremely difficult. There were nine retirements. "It's just a matter of timing," Komatsu said of Bearman's contract extension. "It's just a matter of finalising certain details. But it is our intention to continue with Ollie. The formal announcement will come in due course." The next race is a home one for Haas, the US Grand Prix at Austin's Circuit of the Americas in Texas next week.

item.title: No breakthrough in talks at Antofagasta's striking Centinela copper mine, unions say
item.description: Negotiations between Antofagasta Minerals and two striking unions at Chile's Centinela copper mine showed no progress on Thursday, while three workers marked their seventh day on a hunger strike.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Negotiations between Antofagasta Minerals and two striking unions at Chile's Centinela copper mine showed no progress on Thursday, while three workers marked their seventh day on a hunger strike. The Distrito Centinela and Minera Esperanza unions, which together represent more than 700 workers, began the [USN:L1N45T0DW TEXT:"walkout on October 7"] after contract talks collapsed. The sides returned to the negotiating table on Tuesday in an effort to resolve the dispute. "So far, after three days of voluntary mediation, the company has refused to address a mechanism to end discrimination during the term of the collective agreement," the unions said in a statement. The unions added that the company was continuing to present a financial offer already rejected by workers, while ignoring what they called the core issue: alleged violations of workers' fundamental rights to equal treatment and non-discrimination. The unions say the dispute centers on alleged disparities in pay and benefits for workers performing similar roles at the mine. Antofagasta said on Wednesday that it had so far managed to [USN:S0N44M02N TEXT:"keep production running"] as planned. On Thursday, the company reported a 7% rise in [USN:L1N46106S TEXT:"third-quarter output"] and maintained its full-year production forecast of 625,000 to 655,000 metric tons of copper. In a statement on Thursday, the firm reaffirmed its willingness to seek an agreement, and said dialogue this week has opened up the possibility to reach a deal. The company said it opposed the use of a hunger strike that could put workers' health and lives at risk. The strike at Centinela — along with the ultimately [USN:L1N4600CR TEXT:"averted risk"] of a supervisors' stoppage at Escondida — has helped support global copper prices, amid concerns of difficulties to expand supply enough to meet expected future demand.

item.title: US Justice Dept sues California to block votes from alleged noncitizens
item.description: The US Justice Department sued California on Thursday, asking a federal judge to block the state from counting mail ballots for the November 3 midterm elections from more than 20,000 voters the Trump administration alleges are likely noncitizens.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Goudsward, Luc Cohen
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department sued California on Thursday, asking a federal judge to block the state from counting mail ballots for the November 3 midterm elections from more than 20,000 voters the Trump administration alleges are likely noncitizens. The lawsuit marks the latest effort by President Donald Trump 's administration to boost the federal government's role in elections ahead of the midterms, with his Republican Party locked in a tight battle to retain control of both houses of Congress. The US Constitution assigns the responsibility of administering elections to individual states, though the federal government has some oversight role. Trump has repeatedly claimed that voting by noncitizens - which is illegal - is widespread, despite multiple studies showing it is rare. A Reuters investigation published in July found that just 129 people had been prosecuted for noncitizen voting since the statute criminalizing it passed in 1996. The Justice Department has [USN:L6N45F10R TEXT:"ramped up"] such prosecutions in recent months. In the lawsuit filed in federal court in Los Angeles, the Justice Department sought a court order preventing California from "tabulating in federal elections vote-by-mail ballots received" from more than 20,000 voters until their immigration status is verified. [USN:L6N46002O TEXT:"Reuters previously reported"] that the department sent California a letter giving it a 48-hour deadline on Tuesday to review the list of alleged noncitizen voters. The list was provided on a thumb drive. CALIFORNIA SAYS DOJ SEEKS CHAOS The lawsuit marks an escalation in the federal government's pressure on state election officials over alleged noncitizen voting. The Justice Department has warned election officials in all 50 states that they could face criminal prosecution if they knowingly allowed noncitizens to remain on their voter rolls or cast ballots. It has sued 30 states and Washington DC for refusing to provide complete voter rolls including voters' sensitive personal data, but has lost 26 of those cases so far without winning one. In Thursday's lawsuit against California, the Justice Department said the Department of Homeland Security had identified the 20,000 alleged noncitizens by comparing voter rolls to its own internal databases. Voting rights activists have expressed concern that many citizens who are naturalized could be wrongly flagged as noncitizens due to outdated DHS data. California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder Dean Logan, who were named as defendants in the lawsuit, did not immediately respond to requests for comment. In a statement on Wednesday about the letter, Weber said California's safeguards against noncitizen voting were robust. "The USDOJ's relentless efforts to unlawfully gain access to states' protected voter data and purge voter rolls serve only to cause chaos and fuel public distrust in our elections," Weber said. NONCITIZENS HAVE BEEN REGISTERED THROUGH ERRORS Though states may have added more than 30,000 noncitizens to their voter rolls since 2000 due to software glitches and clerical errors, Reuters found in September, it was unclear how many had cast a ballot. Experts said the numbers were too small relative to the country’s 170 million registered voters to affect elections. Rick Hasen, a law professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, and an expert on election law, said the DOJ’s request would potentially cause California to violate a federal law barring states from conducting mass purges of voter rolls within 90 days of an election. The Trump administration has argued in another case that such restrictions should not apply to removal of noncitizens because they were not legally authorized to register in the first place. Hasen said the DOJ lawsuit would likely face legal hurdles. “The federal government doesn’t have any business directly telling states what ballots they can or cannot send out or not count,” he said. “I just don’t see the federal authority to do that over a state.”

item.title: Infantino apology fails to sway England, Germany over FIFA future
item.description: Gianni Infantino apologised to the FIFA Council on Thursday, but English and German football chiefs said they remained unconvinced he was fit to continue as president of soccer's world governing body.
item.dc:creator: Iain Axon
item.content:encoded: Gianni Infantino apologised to the FIFA Council on Thursday, but English and German football chiefs said they remained unconvinced he was fit to continue as president of soccer's world governing body. Infantino said he had apologised during the closed meeting for mistakes in communicating and consulting over the now-abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project, but stressed that it had been only a proposal and “in no way a done deal”. "First of all, I apologised for the mistakes that we made in relation to the communication and consultation process related to the FIFA Forward Enterprise project, which then led to many consequences," Infantino said in a video published by FIFA. "But what is important to remember is that it was a proposal, so in no way a done deal." The FFE plan involved creating a company to run the commercial interests of FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, and selling a minority stake to private investors. Infantino said it was intended to generate additional funding for FIFA’s 211 member associations. While Infantino appeared to retain strong support among African officials, opposition from some of Europe’s most influential football associations remained pronounced. German FA president Bernd Neuendorf called for a "complete restart" at FIFA, saying the governance reforms the organisation needed could not be delivered with Infantino in charge. "The first thing is we need reforms. That's true. And everyone knows that," Neuendorf said. "The old administration has to be reformed, and the whole governance has to be reformed. But I'm pretty clear here in this that this is not possible with Gianni. "So we need a complete restart, I think, a political restart." English FA chair Debbie Hewitt said Infantino needed to provide answers to questions raised by FIFA Council members and warned that failure to do so would make him unfit to remain president. "I think the man has to answer those questions," Hewitt said. "And if he doesn't answer those questions, no, he's not fit to be FIFA president." Neuendorf questioned the extent of Infantino’s apology, saying he believed it related primarily to the failure to consult the council rather than to the FFE project itself. "I didn't have the feeling that this apology was because of the FFE project in total," Neuendorf said. "My impression was it was just because it wasn't brought forward to the council and no one was involved." Neuendorf said council members had learned about the project through the media rather than from FIFA's leadership and that representatives from other confederations had also complained about the lack of consultation. "When it came to the FFE project as such, I have the impression that this still was not included when he apologised," he said. QUESTIONS UNANSWERED Hewitt said Infantino’s apparent regret over not consulting the council strengthened the case for releasing the relevant FFE documents to its members. "You have an obligation. We all have an obligation, a fiduciary responsibility to answer the questions that have been put forward," Hewitt said. "He told us to submit those questions. There were so many of them, and now it's up to him to do that and do that in the open way. "If there's nothing to hide, then share (the FFE documents) with us... if you regret it that deeply, please share it with us." The meeting also dealt with calls for reform at FIFA, but Hewitt said meaningful changes could not be made until members understood how the decisions at the centre of recent controversies had been reached. She cited FFE, the decision to suspend the automatic one-match ban imposed on United States forward Folarin Balogun after his World Cup red card, and the FIFA Peace Prize awarded to US President Donald Trump as issues requiring greater scrutiny. "Unless we understand what happened, either it was a massive failing in governance because it wasn't followed or actually the governance was followed, but there was something else that got to what we all felt in there was the wrong decisions," Hewitt said. "So we must understand what happened in order to be able to review it. Otherwise we're guessing." The criticism, however, was not unanimous. Ahmed Yahya, the president of the Football Federation of the Islamic Republic of Mauritania (FFRIM), defended Infantino, saying his leadership had helped develop football around the world, pointing to increased funding for national associations and the expansion of the World Cup to 48 teams. "We (the African nations) believe Gianni is the right person to continue leading football," Yahya said. Asked whether most people wanted Infantino to remain president, he added: "I'm certain. The majority want Gianni to stay."

item.title: CNN, Axios and other publishers join Google's AI news program
item.description: Skydance's CNN, the Financial Times, Axios and other publishers joined Google's AI news program to license their content for generative AI features and explore ways to drive audience engagement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Skydance's (SKYD.N) CNN, the Financial Times, Axios and other publishers joined Google's (GOOGL.O) AI news program to license their content for generative AI features and explore ways to drive audience engagement. The search-engine giant said on Thursday that the program, which started as a pilot last year with partners like The Washington Post, now includes more than 400 publications globally. The deal marks CNN's first partnership since [USN:L4N45S0XK TEXT:"Paramount Skydance completed its acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery"], as CEO David Ellison seeks to position the combined company as a technology-driven media business. As part of these agreements, publishers will provide enhanced content rights, allowing Google to develop new AI features, while Google will pay participating news organizations for their content. Financial terms were not disclosed. "Google's innovation with generative AI has changed how people discover information and content, and now those tools will help us explore new ways to discover and engage audiences," said Sam Felix, CNN's senior vice president of strategic partnerships and business development. Google said the AI features will come with clear attribution and direct links, helping readers to connect with the sources they value. The announcement comes at a time when publishers are [USN:L6N45U0ZF TEXT:"stepping up legal efforts"] to prevent AI companies from using their content without permission to train large language models. News publishers are also grappling with declining referral traffic as search engines roll out AI-generated answers that allow users to consume information without clicking through to websites. CNN said the deal is in line with its strategy to protect its intellectual property, adding that it has multiple commercial partnerships and ongoing discussions with other industry players. The network operates television, streaming and digital news services worldwide, including CNN International and CNN Originals, as well as a direct-to-consumer subscription service and CNN Newsource.

item.title: Yémen-Explosions près du palais présidentiel à Aden, attaqué par les Houthis
item.description: Cinq personnes ont été tuées et seize autres blessées jeudi au Yémen dans une attaque au missile effectuée par les Houthis contre le palais présidentiel à Aden, dans le sud du pays, a déclaré le gouvernement reconnu par la communauté internationale.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cinq personnes ont été tuées et seize autres blessées jeudi au Yémen dans une attaque au missile effectuée par les Houthis contre le palais présidentiel à Aden, dans le sud du pays, a déclaré le gouvernement reconnu par la communauté internationale. Le Premier ministre et les ministres qui se trouvaient sur place n'ont pas été blessés, a précisé par ailleurs le ministre yéménite de l'Information, Moammar al-Eryani. Plusieurs explosions avaient auparavant été signalées par des témoins. Deux représentants du gouvernement ont déclaré à Reuters que les Houthis ont tiré plusieurs missiles en direction du palais présidentiel et que deux officiers de sécurité ont été tués dans l'attaque. Selon l'agence de presse Saba, contrôlée par les Houthis, qui dit citer un responsable militaire, le mouvement armé chiite soutenu par l'Iran a visé un centre de commandement dirigé par des officiers saoudiens ainsi que des dépôts d'armes. L'Arabie saoudite chapeaute depuis 2015 une coalition militaire qui intervient au Yémen contre les Houthis. Une trêve entre les belligérants signée en 2022, parfois fragile, a volé en éclats plus tôt cette année, en marge de la campagne militaire lancée par les Etats-Unis et Israël contre l'Iran. Dénonçant des attaques de Ryad en soutien au gouvernement yéménite, les Houthis, qui contrôlent de larges parts du Yémen dont sa capitale Sanaa (nord-ouest) depuis 2014, ont annoncé en juillet dernier un [USN:L6N43M0MM TEXT:"blocus maritime"] de l'Arabie saoudite puis ont récemment multiplié les attaques contre le royaume, ciblant des sites de la compagnie pétrolière Saudi Aramco, pilier de l'économie saoudienne. Ils ont entrepris cet été de renforcer [USN:L8N4520HR TEXT:"leur contrôle"] sur le détroit de [USN:L8N43T289 TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb"], en mer Rouge, une voie importante pour les livraisons énergétiques mondiales - de même que le détroit d'Ormuz, bloqué de facto par l'Iran en réponse aux bombardements américano-israéliens déclenchés en février dernier. En différents points du Yémen, les affrontements entre les Houthis et les forces pro-gouvernementales se sont intensifiés ces dernières semaines, le gouvernement basé à Aden tentant avec l'appui de l'Arabie saoudite de reprendre des territoires contrôlés par le mouvement chiite armé. Alors que les Houthis ont effectué en septembre une [USN:L8N4530M9 TEXT:"avancée éclair"] le long du littoral du Yémen, prenant la ville de Mokha, dans le sud-ouest du pays, le gouvernement reconnu par la communauté internationale a dit lancer ce mois-ci une "[USN:L8N45Q054 TEXT:"offensive d'envergure"]" pour [USN:L8N45R15C TEXT:"reprendre Sanaa"] et d'autres localités sur les rives de la mer Rouge. Il est difficile d'évaluer pleinement la situation militaire actuelle au Yémen. VINGT ATTAQUES CONTRE L'AÉROPORT DE RYAD Pour sa part, l'Arabie saoudite émet depuis environ une semaine des alertes quotidiennes en raison d'attaques au drone et au missile effectuées par les Houthis, qui ont frappé le week-end dernier l'aéroport international de Ryad à deux reprises, tuant samedi 13 personnes - soit l'attaque la plus meurtrière dans le royaume en une décennie. Les autorités saoudiennes ont déclaré jeudi que les Houthis ont tenté d'attaquer des dizaines de sites - aéroports, ports et infrastructures pétrolières. Au cours d'une conférence de presse, le porte-parole de la coalition militaire sous commandement saoudien intervenant au Yémen a déclaré que les Houthis avaient lancé ce mois-ci 20 attaques contre l'aéroport international de Ryad, tuant au total 17 personnes et en blessant 333 autres. Turki al-Maliki a ajouté que les Houthis s'étaient procuré des équipements militaires de pointe, dont des missiles balistiques et des navettes rapides chargées d'explosifs, grâce à l'aide d'"acteurs régionaux", sans en dire davantage. Des sources au fait de la question ont déclaré à Reuters le mois dernier que la prise de la ville de Mokha avait été réalisée par les Houthis grâce à des [USN:L8N4521P7 TEXT:"conseils stratégiques"] donnés par les Gardiens iraniens de la révolution. Téhéran admet de longue date que les Houthis sont des alliés mais dément leur donner de quelconques directives militaires. Le Yémen est en conflit depuis que les Houthis ont saisi la capitale Sanaa en 2014. Si elle a un temps permis de stopper les hostilités à grande échelle, la trêve supervisée par les Nations unies en 2022 n'a pas débouché sur une issue politique en dépit de plusieurs cycles de pourparlers, avant que l'intensification des tensions régionales ne plombent quelque processus de paix.

item.title: Home of MLB's Blue Jays swaps bats for clubs as ballpark transforms into nine-hole golf course
item.description: Home runs will be swapped for holes-in-one at the home of Major League Baseball's Toronto Blue Jays when the domed stadium is transformed into a temporary nine-hole golf course in January with shots launched from the stands at greens on the field below.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Home runs will be swapped for holes-in-one at the home of Major League Baseball's Toronto Blue Jays when the domed stadium is transformed into a temporary nine-hole golf course in January with shots launched from the stands at greens on the field below. From January 20 to 24, golfers will have the chance to hit from tee blocks set up on various levels of the stadium where last year the Los Angeles Dodgers won a second consecutive [USN:L1N3WB142 TEXT:"World Series"]. A shot that lands on the designated green counts as a par, and one that misses is carded as a bogey. A birdie is awarded when a ball finishes inside the inner circle around the pin, while a hole-in-one, the golfer's version of a home run, is left to the lucky few who can pull it off. "This unique event reimagines Rogers Centre as a golf destination unlike any other, inviting players of all skill levels and ages to experience one of Canada's most iconic sports and entertainment landmarks like never before," Marnie Starkman, executive vice president of business operations for the Toronto Blue Jays, said in a press release. Golfers, who will be provided with clubs at each tee box, will start their 90-minute round at the venue's 200 Level and make their way through the ballpark, finishing on the 500 Level. Standard tee times start at C$125 ($88.04) per person. ($1 = 1.4198 Canadian dollars)

item.title: Nasdaq resolves network disruption that caused data gaps, source says
item.description: Nasdaq , home to some of the biggest US tech companies, experienced a network disruption at its Carteret, New Jersey facility that caused intermittent data gaps across all of its US equities markets on Thursday, though a person familiar with the matter said the blips have ceased in recent hours.
item.dc:creator: Pritam Biswas
item.content:encoded: Nasdaq (NDAQ.O) , home to some of the biggest US tech companies, experienced a network disruption at its Carteret, New Jersey facility that caused intermittent data gaps across all of its US equities markets on Thursday, though a person familiar with the matter said the blips have ceased in recent hours. The disruption was a routine network issue rather than a fundamental failure of the exchange operator's internal systems and had no impact on actual trading, the person said. The company had issued an alert at 11:27:50 a.m. ET saying the incident affected multiple multicast groups and impacted both hardware and software feeds for Nasdaq, Nasdaq Texas and Nasdaq PSX. Both the primary "A" and secondary "B" feeds originating from the Carteret facility had been compromised, it said. Nasdaq advised clients to switch their systems to unaffected backup feeds originating from its Chicago facility to ensure market access. The exchange operator also instructed clients experiencing data gaps to submit recovery requests for any missing data, and said it was "actively investigating the issue." Networking gaps on exchanges can roil markets, dampen traders' confidence and attract scrutiny from the Securities and Exchange Commission. While Nasdaq's electronic platforms are typically reliable, the exchange operator has faced several notable issues in recent years that briefly affected market activity. Shares of Nasdaq, which lists Apple (AAPL.O) , Tesla (TSLA.O) and Nvidia (NVDA.O) among thousands of other companies, were unaffected by the network disruption. They have fallen about 3.8% so far in 2026.

item.title: Rendimientos en EEUU caen, inversionistas buscan refugio y apuestan por una pausa en alza tasas
item.description: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro estadounidense a más largo plazo cayeron el jueves a sus niveles más bajos desde septiembre, debido a la preocupación por la desaceleración del crecimiento de la IA y a las apuestas de que la Fed mantendrá las tasas sin cambios en su próxima reunión.
item.dc:creator: Sinead Carew
item.content:encoded: Los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro estadounidense a más largo plazo cayeron el jueves a sus niveles más bajos desde septiembre, debido a la preocupación por la desaceleración del crecimiento de la IA y a las apuestas de que la Fed mantendrá las tasas sin cambios en su próxima reunión. * Tras conocerse unos datos de ventas minoristas y de inflación mayorista superiores a lo esperado, los rendimientos redujeron brevemente sus caídas antes de reanudar el descenso iniciado durante la sesión asiática, y los retornos a 10 y 30 años alcanzaron sus niveles más bajos desde el 23 de septiembre. * Las ventas minoristas de Estados Unidos en septiembre aumentaron más de lo esperado debido al alza de los precios de la gasolina, pero el gasto en otros ámbitos fue moderado, lo que podría atenuar las expectativas de otro trimestre de sólido crecimiento del gasto de los consumidores. * Los precios al productor, en tanto, anotaron en septiembre su mayor subida en cuatro años y medio, en un contexto de aumento de los costos de bienes y servicios, lo que constituye el último indicio de que la elevada inflación se está extendiendo más allá de los productos energéticos. * El repunte de la demanda de bonos del Tesoro coincidió con las caídas previas de las acciones tecnológicas (.SPLRCT) , ya que los inversionistas huían de los valores de IA, muy endeudados, que han sido los responsables de gran parte del crecimiento del mercado bursátil en los últimos años. * Mientras, la presidenta de la Reserva Federal de San Francisco, Mary Daly, fue la última autoridad en abogar por una pausa en las subidas de tasas. Daly dijo tarde el miércoles que la Fed probablemente tendrá que aumentar aún más las tasas de interés a corto plazo para frenar una inflación demasiado elevada, pero señaló que no es necesario hacerlo en la reunión del banco central estadounidense del 27 al 28 de octubre. * El rendimiento a 10 años cayó 10,1 puntos básicos al 5,089% tras alcanzar su nivel más bajo desde el 23 de septiembre. El rendimiento de referencia marcó su mayor baja diaria desde inicios de agosto de 2025 y su mayor descenso en tres días desde principios de septiembre de 2025. * El retorno a 30 años cedió 9,8 puntos básicos, al 5,426%. Tras tocar su nivel más bajo desde el 23 de septiembre, anotó hacia su mayor caída diaria desde el 10 de octubre de 2025 y su mayor descenso en cinco días desde principios de septiembre del año pasado. * La rentabilidad a dos años , que suele evolucionar en línea con las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés de la Fed, cayó 5,3 puntos básicos al 4,749%. Tras tocar su mínimo desde el 18 de septiembre, marcó su caída más pronunciada en un solo día desde el 1 de octubre.

item.title: El S&P 500 cierra en alza; los inversores se pasan de la inteligencia artificial al sector de salud
item.description: El S&P 500 cerró con un alza el jueves, recuperándose de pérdidas iniciales, ya que los inversores, preocupados por las acciones del sector de la inteligencia artificial (IA), se decantaron por Eli Lilly, UnitedHealth y otras de los sectores de salud y de consumo.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich, Sruthi Shankar
item.content:encoded: El S&P 500 cerró con un alza el jueves, recuperándose de pérdidas iniciales, ya que los inversores, preocupados por las acciones del sector de la inteligencia artificial (IA), se decantaron por Eli Lilly, UnitedHealth y otras de los sectores de salud y de consumo. Varias acciones tecnológicas cayeron, ya que los inversores analizaron con detenimiento las empresas relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial, cuyo alto endeudamiento las hace vulnerables a las subidas de las tasas de interés. Las acciones de Eli Lilly (LLY.N) , UnitedHealth (UNH.N) y Walmart repuntaron después de que Deutsche Bank revisó al alza sus recomendaciones. Broadcom (AVGO.O) y Nvidia (NVDA.O) bajaron después de que el fabricante de chips TSMC (2330.TW) se mostró cauto sobre 2027, a pesar de reportar por sexto trimestre consecutivo una ganancia récord gracias a la sólida demanda impulsada por la inteligencia artificial. Dell Technologies (DELL.N) y Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE.N) profundizaron las fuertes pérdidas de la sesión anterior, debido a la preocupación por las empresas de IA expuestas a unos costos de financiamiento más altos. El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro a 10 años retrocedió, pero se mantuvo cerca de máximos de varios años, ya que a los inversores les preocupa la inflación relacionada con los altos precios del petróleo. "El costo de financiar cualquier cosa, ya sea una nueva vivienda unifamiliar o un gigantesco centro de datos, está aumentando, y eso tiene implicaciones para muchos aspectos del mercado bursátil", dijo Jed Ellerbroek, gestor de carteras de Argent Capital Management. "Las acciones con mejor rendimiento hoy son las de empresas defensivas y no cíclicas". El índice de semiconductores de Filadelfia (.SOX) cayó por séptima sesión consecutiva. Según datos preliminares, el S&P 500 (.SPX) subió 24,94 puntos, un 0,32%, a 7.744,07 unidades; el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) ganó 18,37 puntos, un 0,07%, a 26.711,24 unidades; el Promedio Industrial Dow Jones (.DJI) sumó 559,45 puntos, o un 1,08%, a 52.180,93 unidades.

item.title: Factores externos complican andar de mercados financieros de Argentina
item.description: La firmeza del crudo y la presión inflacionaria en Estados Unidos impactaron lateralmente el jueves los activos del mercado financiero de Argentina, cuyo riesgo país se sostiene por encima de los 600 puntos básicos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La firmeza del crudo y la presión inflacionaria en Estados Unidos impactaron lateralmente el jueves los activos del mercado financiero de Argentina, cuyo riesgo país se sostiene por encima de los 600 puntos básicos. El prolongado conflicto bélico en Oriente Medio hace que el petróleo cotice por arriba de los 100 dólares el barril, lo que golpea los precios minoristas estadounidenses, una situación que eleva la probabilidad de un nuevo incremento en las tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal (Fed). "Los inversores incrementan su prudencia porque el frente internacional no pinta nada bien. A la firmeza del crudo se suma la posible nueva alza de tasas por parte de la Fed, dos temas que perjudican a los mercados emergentes, quitan liquidez y aumentan los costos de financiamiento", explicó un analista de un banco de capitales españoles con negocios domésticos. El riesgo país de Argentina trepaba con firmeza a los 623 puntos básicos (2000 GMT), un nivel similar al alcanzado a inicios de mes, lo que desalienta el armado de carteras en general. Sin embargo, algunas compras selectivas de oportunidad dejaron una ronda con altibajos intradiarios y reacomodamientos específicos. Los títulos públicos extrabursátiles pasaron a quedar con un ligero sesgo positivo del 0,1% en promedio, contra un derrumbe del 1,2% previo, al tiempo que las acciones mediante el índice líder S&P Merval (.MERV) porteño ganaron un 0,82% al cierre, desde el 1,16% negativo del miércoles. Ambos mercados abrieron en baja y profundizaron esta tendencia cuando el riesgo país llegó a marcar unas 640 unidades luego del mediodía local. Mientras tanto, en la franja cambiaria se observó al peso mayorista estable en las 1.513,5 unidades por dólar , contra una compra diaria de 182 millones de dólares por parte del banco central (BCRA). Estas intervenciones oficiales suman 574 millones de dólares en los últimos tres días. El [USN:L1N4600OU TEXT:"Tesoro"] argentino viene de colocar títulos por un valor efectivo de 6,61 billones de pesos (unos 4.367,4 millones de dólares) en una licitación interna para refinanciar vencimientos de corto plazo. Esta operatoria recibió un total de ofertas por 9,49 billones de pesos y abarcó una renovación (rollover) del 136,14% de los vencimientos previstos. Operadores dijeron que el Tesoro habría realizado una operación de compra de bonos por 1 billón de pesos, lo que ayudaría reducir el impacto de la absorción de la última licitación. Fuentes del mercado no descartan que Argentina pueda utilizar el "swap" de divisas con China en caso de no poder refinanciarse los "Bonares" en 2027 por un contexto global adverso y una continua búsqueda de superávit fiscal. "Para que se cumpla la meta de superávit primario, el gasto nacional no automático debería caer un 6% anual en los últimos meses de 2026", dijo un informe del Instituto de Estudios Económicos sobre la Realidad Argentina y Latinoamericana (IERAL) de Fundación Mediterránea. Y acotó que la recaudación nacional mostró una recuperación en septiembre, aunque todavía acumula una caída en términos reales durante 2026. El Gobierno dijo en julio que, dentro del programa financiero 2027, estaba prevista la emisión de unos 5.000 millones de dólares en "Bonares" como parte de la estrategia de financiamiento de ese año.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis hit palace in Aden, coalition details attacks on Saudi infrastructure
item.description: Yemen's Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing five people, the government said, as the Saudi-led coalition listed dozens of Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure in recent weeks.
item.dc:creator: Enas Alashray, Mohammed Ghobari, Eman Abouhassira
item.content:encoded: Yemen's Houthis fired missiles at the presidential palace complex in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing five people, the government said, as the Saudi-led coalition listed dozens of Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure in recent weeks. The attack was the first in the current conflict between the Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi Arabia on Aden's Al-Maashiq palace, the seat of Yemen's Saudi-backed and internationally recognised government. The conflict is a new theatre in the wider regional war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Yemen's prime minister and cabinet members were safe following the attack, Yemeni Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said. Witnesses told Reuters they heard loud booms near the palace. Yemen's cabinet said the attack involved missiles and drones. Yemen's health minister Qasim Buhaibeh said five people were killed and 16 wounded in what he described as a Houthi attack on the government's official headquarters at the presidential complex. The casualties included guards and civilian employees. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said its fighters had bombed what he described as the Saudi military operations headquarters in Aden, as part of the group's declared policy of targeting "Saudi reinforcements wherever they were located". The Houthi-run news agency SABA said the headquarters was run by Saudi officers and that there were weapons depots there. Reuters could not independently verify the claims. Fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed forces resumed last month, and aid agencies [USN:L6N4600ML TEXT:"have warned"] of rapidly worsening conditions in Yemen. Last week, government forces launched a campaign to recapture areas controlled by the Houthis, recovering ground near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping artery. War broke out in Yemen in 2014 when [USN:L1N45Q02Z TEXT:"the Houthis"] seized the capital Sanaa, driving the government south. A Saudi-led military intervention the following year led to a bloody stalemate before a 2022 truce that held until this year. In that phase of the conflict Houthi fighters and allied forces briefly seized Al-Maashiq palace during a battle for Aden, before withdrawing. COALITION SAYS HOUTHIS ARE GETTING MISSILES, FAST BOATS As Saudi Arabia backs government forces, the Houthis [USN:L1N4610L5 TEXT:"have been firing"] ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports, ports and oil installations, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a [USN:L1N46108L TEXT:"pressure point"] in the wider war [USN:L6N45Y0GN TEXT:"and threatening"] its ambitious economic plans. On Thursday, the Saudi-led military coalition said the Houthis had attempted to attack dozens of such sites, highlighting the risk to Saudi civilian infrastructure. The governing council of the UN's International Civil Aviation Organization condemned the recent attacks on civilian airports, aircraft, and aviation infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki told reporters that the Houthis had launched 20 attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh this month, killing 17 people and wounding 333 others. The airport is one of Saudi Arabia's main international aviation hubs. The coalition said Houthi attacks on Abha airport in southwestern Saudi Arabia near the Yemeni border had killed three people and wounded 28. Maliki said the Houthis had acquired advanced military technology with the help of "regional actors," including ballistic missiles, drones and explosive-laden fast boats. Iran [USN:L1N43P0D6 TEXT:"has provided"] weapons, money and training to the Houthis, although Tehran has officially denied arming them in violation of a UN arms embargo. Maliki also said the coalition had destroyed 127 weapons storage facilities and launch platforms in Yemen's mountainous areas, calling on the Houthis to immediately halt operations targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure. Shortly afterwards, the Houthi military spokesperson said Saudi airspace and airports were unsafe, renewing a warning to airlines while excluding airspace over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina. Saudi Arabia's civil defence authority issued early-warning alerts throughout Thursday over potential threats in the cities of Najran and Jizan, as well as the wider Najran and Jazan regions, before later saying the danger had passed. The Saudi-led coalition said on Thursday that it had intercepted and destroyed a drone in the southwestern Saudi Arabian city of Khamis Mushait, and another launched towards the country's southern region.

item.title: Trump rechaza plan de Hegseth de transmitir en directo la ejecución de condenado a muerte
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, descartó el jueves los planes de transmitir en directo el fusilamiento de un excomandante del Ejército, desestimando la propuesta del jefe del Pentágono, Pete Hegseth, tras la oposición de republicanos, líderes religiosos y la opinión pública.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, descartó el jueves los planes de transmitir en directo el fusilamiento de un excomandante del Ejército, desestimando la propuesta del jefe del Pentágono, Pete Hegseth, tras la oposición de republicanos, líderes religiosos y la opinión pública. Este cambio de rumbo puso fin al plan de emitir el fusilamiento de Nidal Hasan, condenado por matar a 13 personas en Fort Hood, prevista para el 3 de diciembre. También supuso un inusual desacuerdo público entre Trump y uno de sus aliados más cercanos, aunque el Pentágono afirmó que ambos estaban "totalmente de acuerdo". Hegseth había anunciado planes para retransmitir en directo la ejecución en la base militar de Fort Hood, en Texas, lugar donde Hasan perpetró el atentado de 2009. No se conoce ningún otro país que televise o transmita en directo ejecuciones judiciales. Trump y sus asesores no estaban al corriente del plan de transmisión en directo, según afirmó un funcionario de la Casa Blanca que habló bajo condición de anonimato. "Creo que transmitir la ejecución para que todos la vean podría haber sido un fuerte elemento disuasorio para que el mundo fuera testigo de cómo Estados Unidos se enfrenta a terroristas y escoria como Hasan, pero muchas personas muy buenas y bienintencionadas preferirían no verlo morir, ya sea a través de una transmisión en directo o de cualquier otro dispositivo visual", escribió Trump en una publicación en las redes sociales. "Morirá, tal y como está previsto, fusilado, pero este acto no se transmitirá". Las familias de las víctimas de Hasan podrán presenciar la ejecución en persona si así lo desean, tal y como es habitual en las ejecuciones en Estados Unidos. Algunos compañeros republicanos de Trump, entre ellos el vicepresidente JD Vance, así como líderes religiosos, habían expresado desde dudas hasta una condena rotunda del plan del Pentágono de transmitir en directo. Las encuestas de opinión revelaron que la mayoría de los estadounidenses se oponía a la retransmisión en directo. El arzobispo Timothy Broglio, responsable de la atención espiritual de los miembros católicos de las Fuerzas Armadas de Estados Unidos, también planteó objeciones, mientras que el papa León condenó la pena capital en todas sus formas. No fue posible contactar de inmediato con un abogado que representara a Hasan para recabar sus comentarios, y no estaba claro si la fecha de ejecución prevista para el 3 de diciembre se vería retrasada por recursos legales. DESACUERDO CON HEGSETH Se trató de la primera gran ruptura pública de Trump con Hegseth, un aliado suyo. Sin embargo, no estaba claro si esta ruptura pondría en peligro políticamente a Hegseth, dados sus fuertes lazos. En un comunicado, el Pentágono afirmó que Trump había hablado con Hegseth sobre la decisión antes de anunciarla en Truth Social. "El secretario respalda la decisión del presidente, y ambos están totalmente de acuerdo", declaró el portavoz jefe del Pentágono, Sean Parnell, en un comunicado. La pena capital en Estados Unidos ya se enfrentaba a un renovado escrutinio después de que [USN:L8N45N1T5 TEXT:"Christa Pike"], condenada por asesinato en la década de los noventa, sobreviviera a dos inyecciones letales en un intento fallido de ejecución por parte de Tennessee el mes pasado, que la dejó gravemente herida y requirió su hospitalización. "GRAVES CONSECUENCIAS" Un jurado militar condenó a Hasan, un antiguo psiquiatra del Ejército de los Estados Unidos, por asesinato premeditado tras matar a tiros a 13 soldados desarmados e herir a otros 32 en un centro médico de la extensa base. Las fuerzas del orden dispararon a Hasan durante su ataque, dejándolo paralizado de cintura para abajo, y ahora se desplaza en silla de ruedas. Hegseth había afirmado que la transmisión de la ejecución era necesaria para garantizar que la gente comprendiera que "este tipo de actos acarrean graves consecuencias". Las elecciones de mitad de legislatura del 3 de noviembre determinarán si los republicanos conservan el control del Congreso, en un momento en que los votantes muestran cada vez más su desaprobación hacia las políticas de Trump en las encuestas de opinión. El senador John Curtis, republicano por Utah, calificó la cancelación de "la decisión acertada" en un comunicado. El diputado estadounidense Richard Neal, demócrata por Massachusetts, calificó el plan original de "un profundo fracaso del juicio moral y de la decencia humana básica".

item.title: Nvidia, Apple each gave $25 million for Trump's ballroom, Washington Post reports
item.description: Nvidia and Apple each committed $25 million for US President Donald Trump's planned White House ballroom, according to a Washington Post report on Thursday that showed $333 million in private donations for the project.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Apple (AAPL.O) each committed $25 million for US President Donald Trump's planned White House ballroom, according to a Washington Post report on Thursday that showed $333 million in private donations for the project. The Adelson family, longtime financial supporters of Trump and his Republican Party, committed $25 million as well, as did billionaire Charles Ergen, co-founder and chairman of telecommunications company Dish Network, the report added. The president himself is not on the list, according to the Post. Reuters has not verified the report. The White House said it would not release information about the donors, who spokesman Davis Ingle said "represent a wide array of great American companies." "The same critics who are alleging fake conflicts of interests would also complain if American taxpayers were footing the bill for these long-overdue renovations," Ingle told Reuters. Nvidia said it was proud to make a donation to a nonpartisan trust that serves Americans. "As an American company, our support for the United States is paramount, and independent of any business interests," a spokesperson said. Apple declined to comment. The scale of the ballroom project and the administration’s handling of fundraising and disclosures have drawn criticism from watchdog groups and legal experts, who say they raise questions about transparency, donor influence and adherence to longstanding ethics and oversight norms. "The secrecy is a huge problem," said Eric Petry of the Brennan Center for Justice. "When people with business before the government can give millions to the president's pet project, and the public can't see who or how much, there's no way to tell whether they're buying access or favors." Federal contractors including Lockheed Martin Corp, Microsoft Corp and Palantir Technologies Inc all gave $10 million, the Post reported. The companies did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Trump initially said he and wealthy donors would pay for the estimated $400 million project, but he later unsuccessfully sought $1 billion from Congress for an underground bunker and security features to harden the facility. The Post reported that the "vast majority of the funds raised came from companies and wealthy individuals with interests before the federal government" and that half the total came from companies or executives of firms that have had federal government contracts in Trump's second White House term. The planned ballroom is among [USN:L1N3YZ1G0 TEXT:"several projects"] Trump is pursuing in his efforts to remake Washington with sweeping, unilateral changes that his opponents have challenged in court and called a power grab. The US Supreme Court, in a 5-4 [USN:S0N42U037 TEXT:"ruling"] in August, allowed Trump to continue construction of the ballroom while he challenges a judicial order that would halt much of the development. In a dissent, Chief Justice John Roberts said the project was "likely unlawful." The ballroom, which Trump has said will seat 1,000 guests, has faced public backlash. Preservationists and opponents say Trump exceeded his authority by demolishing the historic East Wing, which housed the first lady's offices and the White House movie theater, to make room for the structure. Trump says a planned 90,000-square-foot (8,360-square-meter) White House ballroom will include bomb shelters, medical facilities, defenses against drones and missiles and other security features. Confronted with criticism of the project, his administration now says the facility is needed for national security, an argument the president has also made about a proposed triumphal arch.

item.title: Huracán Trudy se intensifica frente a costa del Pacífico mexicano
item.description: El huracán Trudy se intensificaba rápidamente sobre el océano Pacífico, a medida que se acercaba a la costa occidental de México, amenazando con dejar más lluvias y fuertes vientos en una zona castigada en las últimas semanas por varios ciclones tropicales que han causado inundaciones y algunos muertos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El huracán Trudy se intensificaba rápidamente sobre el océano Pacífico, a medida que se acercaba a la costa occidental de México, amenazando con dejar más lluvias y fuertes vientos en una zona castigada en las últimas semanas por varios ciclones tropicales que han causado inundaciones y algunos muertos. A las 11.00 hora local (1700 GMT), el ciclón se ubicaba a unos 430 kilómetros al sur-suroeste del puerto Acapulco, en el estado Guerrero, y soplaba vientos máximos sostenidos de 150 kilómetros por hora (km/h), con ráfagas más fuertes, mientras avanzaba hacia el norte-noroeste a 9 km/h, según datos del Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos (NHC, por su sigla en inglés). Se espera que Trudy se siga intensificando hasta convertirse en un huracán de categoría 4 en la escala de Saffir-Simpson. Un ciclón de ese nivel puede soplar vientos máximos sostenidos de hasta 250 km/h y causar daños generalizados en estructuras protectoras, desplome de tejados en edificios pequeños, erosión de bancales y playas e inundaciones en terrenos interiores. "Si Trudy se intensifica como se pronostica, los fuertes vientos cerca de su centro generarán olas peligrosamente altas en alta mar. El oleaje se extenderá hacia afuera, amenazando tanto a embarcaciones pequeñas como a grandes buques", advirtió AccuWeather, una compañía estadounidense de servicios comerciales de pronóstico del tiempo. Si bien no se prevé que Trudy toque tierra, descargaría fuertes lluvias en la franja costera que va desde el conocido destino turístico Acapulco hasta Puerto Vallarta, pasando por los dos mayores puertos del país; Lázaro Cárdenas y Manzanillo. En las últimas semanas, la misma zona ya fue golpeada por los huracanes [USN:L6N45L0YK TEXT:"Polo"] y [USN:L8N45V0SM TEXT:"Simón"]. Si bien este último tampoco tocó tierra, sigue activo, aunque como tormenta tropical, frente a la costa del Pacífico mexicano.

item.title: Manchester City march on with title charge clouded by financial case
item.description: Manchester City will attempt to keep their perfect Premier League start rolling at home to Ipswich Town on Saturday, with uncertainty over their punishment for financial rule breaches continuing to hang over the leaders.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Manchester City will attempt to keep their perfect Premier League start rolling at home to Ipswich Town on Saturday, with uncertainty over their punishment for financial rule breaches continuing to hang over the leaders. Enzo Maresca's City have won their opening six league games and sit three points clear of Arsenal, making a fine start on the pitch while their future off it remains unresolved. An independent commission found City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League. City have denied wrongdoing and [USN:L1N45O0BQ TEXT:"lodged an appeal"]. The extraordinary backdrop has done little to derail City's domestic campaign. They underlined their strength with a 3-0 [USN:L1N45X053 TEXT:"victory at 10-man Liverpool"] last Sunday. The did lose 4-2 at home to [USN:L1N46011B TEXT:"holders Paris St Germain"] in the Champions League on Wednesday but return to the Etihad Stadium to face an Ipswich side sitting 10th on nine points. Former Manchester United defender Gary Neville said the uncertainty over City's eventual punishment had created wider frustration around the league, with the club continuing to win while the significance of those victories, with potential sanctions still to come, remained unclear. "This is not good for the Premier League, this is really bad for the Premier League — it's going to continue for a few months," Neville said on Sky Sports. "Up and down the country, (there's) a lot of annoyance that they see this team win football matches; it's just not going to be enjoyed." For champions Arsenal, who demolished Lille 3-0 in the Champions League on Tuesday, there is little room to surrender points if they are to keep pace in the title race. The London side sit second on 15 points and visit Nottingham Forest on Sunday knowing any slip could allow City to open a significant early gap. Forest are 15th with five points. SPECTACULAR LIVERPOOL VICTORY Liverpool will arrive at Brentford on Saturday with a different kind of momentum after a spectacular 6-3 Champions League victory at LASK on Wednesday. The night in Austria belonged to [USN:L8N4602A7 TEXT:"Bradley Barcola"], whose hat-trick represented his first goals for Liverpool after going scoreless in his opening six appearances for the club. The French forward, whose frustrating start with the Reds had drawn increasing scrutiny, struck twice before halftime and completed his treble after the break as Liverpool made it two wins from two in the Champions League. It was a badly needed breakthrough for 24-year-old Barcola and a welcome response from Liverpool after their humbling home defeat by City four days earlier. Liverpool have been far less convincing domestically, however. They are ninth on nine points and face a Brentford side sitting a point above them in fourth, meaning Saturday could provide a sterner examination of whether the Reds' nine-goal European thriller has genuinely shifted their momentum. Manchester United's problems are more acute as they make the short trip to Elland Road to face Leeds United on Sunday desperate to breathe life into a troubled campaign. Michael Carrick's side have collected six points from their opening six games and sit 13th, already 12 points behind City after their worst start in 40 years. United slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday and their latest assignment carries an additional edge against old rivals Leeds, who have made the stronger start and sit seventh with nine points. Three teams are still searching for their first victory, including bottom side Fulham who welcome Hull City on Saturday, Bournemouth who host Sunderland on Sunday and Tottenham Hotspur who are at home to Coventry City on Monday. With Manchester City trying to shut out the noise around their financial case, Arsenal determined to stay on their heels and Liverpool and United searching for a revival, the weekend should help show how the traditional heavyweights are coping.

item.title: Dólar cae desde máximo de 18 meses porque alza de bonos modera preocupación por la inflación
item.description: El dólar retrocedió el jueves desde un máximo de 18 meses, porque los inversores miraron más allá de los sólidos datos de inflación y gasto en Estados Unidos para centrarse en la caída de los valores de las empresas de centros de datos de inteligencia artificial.
item.dc:creator: Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: El dólar retrocedió el jueves desde un máximo de 18 meses, porque los inversores miraron más allá de los sólidos datos de inflación y gasto en Estados Unidos para centrarse en la caída de los valores de las empresas de centros de datos de inteligencia artificial. * Los precios al productor en Estados Unidos registraron en septiembre su mayor aumento en cuatro años y medio debido al alza en los costos de bienes y servicios, lo que refuerza la evidencia de que las presiones inflacionarias se están extendiendo a otros sectores desde el energético. * Las ventas minoristas aumentaron más de lo previsto, impulsadas por los precios más altos de la gasolina, mientras que las solicitudes semanales de subsidio por desempleo subieron levemente, apuntando a una demanda de los consumidores resiliente y a un mercado laboral estable. * Sin embargo, el precio de los bonos gubernamentales repuntó y el dólar retrocedió, reflejando comentarios cautos de autoridades monetarias de la Reserva Federal que enfriaron aún más las expectativas de un alza de las tasas de interés en octubre. * "Tenemos una narrativa negativa para el dólar basada en la idea de que la inflación a este nivel y a este ritmo acelerado es insostenible", dijo Juan Pérez, director de operaciones de Monex USA en Washington. * "A pesar de las malas noticias en el frente de guerra y del panorama bursátil pesimista, el mercado se muestra contrario al dólar tras un fuerte repunte en las últimas cuatro semanas (...) El estancamiento económico parece estar influyendo cada vez más en la opinión de los operadores", agregó. * El índice dólar , que compara al billete verde con una cesta de seis destacadas divisas, cayó un 0,45%, a 101,99 unidades, tras haber alcanzado el miércoles un máximo en 18 meses después de que las cifras de inflación en Estados Unidos resultaron más altas de lo esperado. * El euro repuntó un 0,56% desde un mínimo de 18 meses, a 1,1218 dólares, para su mayor avance diario en casi dos meses. La libra esterlina ganó un 0,64%, a 1,3275 dólares, tras datos que mostraron que la economía británica creció un 0,1% en agosto. * El yen se fortaleció un 0,15%, a 158,08 unidades por dólar.

item.title: CoreWeave's slump spotlights growing burden of debt behind AI boom
item.description: Shares of Nvidia-backed CoreWeave steadied on Thursday after a sharp slump, as investors worried about the debt financing behind the artificial intelligence build-out.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Soni, Anhata Rooprai, Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: Shares of Nvidia-backed CoreWeave (CRWV.O) steadied on Thursday after a sharp slump, as investors worried about the debt financing behind the artificial intelligence build-out. The loss-making cloud company has about $50 billion in debt and has become a focus of concerns that the data-center boom is being fueled by credit, straining newer players and pressuring cash flows even at giants such as Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Meta Platforms (META.O) . CoreWeave's slump fueled a global rout in AI stocks, underscoring investor doubts about whether future revenue from the technology can keep pace with the spending. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company is CoreWeave's second-largest investor with about a 10% stake, played down the fears. "CoreWeave’s financial strength is improving every day," Huang told reporters at a Stockholm event, adding that he does not see a need for Nvidia to backstop the company. "I'm optimistic. Their cost of capital is actually decreasing." CoreWeave stock was last up 5% after slipping as much as 8.3% to its lowest level since May 2025. "The market is waking up to the fact that AI demand and a profitable business model are two very different things," said Axel Rudolph, chief technical analyst at IG Group. "It looks more like investors questioning how the build-out is being funded than a sudden collapse in appetite for AI computing. But if the cost of capital keeps rising, even strong demand may not be enough to protect the most heavily leveraged players." The jitters come as [USN:L6N4601DE TEXT:"investors await Anthropic's IPO"], which would be a test of whether the Claude AI model maker's rapid revenue growth can ease worries about runaway AI spending. The market selloff has already led some companies such as [USN:L4N45L0SK TEXT:"smart ring maker Oura"] (OURA.O) to [USN:L4N45V00M TEXT:"push back their listings"]. The yield on CoreWeave's April-issued bonds was trading around 15% on Thursday, above the level that typically signals distress, drawing a "yikes" from Elon Musk on social media. The bond was last down 0.3 cents on the dollar to 79.15 cents, according to Tradeweb data. The [USN:L1N46104Z TEXT:"cost of insuring its debt"] against default has climbed to around 1,000 basis points, implying a nearly 63% chance of default in five years, up from about 30% a year ago. That is despite a deal under which Nvidia (NVDA.O) will buy any unsold CoreWeave capacity through April 13, 2032. Options traders also ramped up bearish bets. Volume in put options, which give investors the right to sell shares at a certain price, hit a record high on Wednesday, according to Chris Murphy, co-head of derivatives strategy at Susquehanna. “People are using put options to hedge negative credit sentiment, and we've seen consistent and aggressive put buying all week,” Murphy said. Investors bought contracts that would profit if CoreWeave shares fell below $42.50, $50, and $60 in the coming weeks, while others used more complex trades to reduce the cost of some of those bearish wagers by taking on some risk tied to much lower share-price levels later in the year, according to Murphy and TradeAlert data. CoreWeave, [USN:L3N3QB14S TEXT:"which went public in March 2025"], leads newer cloud providers known as neoclouds that rent out computing power from scarce and costly Nvidia processors to meet soaring demand, often borrowing heavily to buy the chips. It counts Microsoft and OpenAI among its customers, according to media reports. That leaves neoclouds exposed to any cooling in AI demand, critics have said, while the chips lose value as newer ones arrive, forcing another round of heavy spending to replace them. CoreWeave [USN:L4N4481ER TEXT:"raised its annual capital spending forecast"] by $4 billion to as much as $39 billion in August. It is expected to post revenue of nearly $13 billion this year and a loss of $2.13 billion, according to analysts' estimates. Worries about the build-out, on which US tech giants are expected to spend more than $700 billion this year, have in recent days rippled through the stocks that have been the biggest winners since ChatGPT's November 2022 launch. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (.SOX) , a closely watched gauge of chip stocks, has erased over $1.6 trillion in market value in an 11.6% slide over the past six sessions. The Nasdaq (.NDX) has declined more than 3% in the period. On Thursday, tech shares fell across Asia, Europe and the US, dragging broader markets lower on fears that rising interest rates could hurt the sector. 'UNLIMITED' POOLS OF CAPITAL The CoreWeave selloff came as its co-founder Brannin McBee told the Financial Times that the company was seeking an investment-grade rating that would open the door to "unlimited" capital. The same day research firm Gartner said about 80% of neoclouds could shut down by 2030 and that more than $3.5 trillion of AI spending could face impairment if AI providers keep up their current pace of investment. "In 2026, AI providers are expected to spend nearly $1 trillion on AI infrastructure, and are forecast to invest an additional $6 trillion between 2027 and 2030," said Will Sommer, analyst at Gartner. "However, our research indicates enterprise and consumer AI revenue will be insufficient to support profitable returns on all planned AI capital expenditures during this period." CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator pushed back on the concerns in an [USN:L4N4601XL TEXT:"internal memo on Wednesday"] seen by Reuters, telling employees the company's deal backlog more than covers its debt obligations and that markets can sometimes "misunderstand and act irrationally".

item.title: TSX rises, touches three-week high
item.description: Canada's main stock index closed higher on Thursday, touching a three-week high, powered by mining and tech stocks as lower bond yields boosted risk appetite, offsetting weakness in energy shares.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index closed higher on Thursday, touching a three-week high, powered by mining and tech stocks as lower bond yields boosted risk appetite, offsetting weakness in energy shares. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) was up 1.55%, at 36,137.10, rebounding after sharp declines in the previous session. Canada's benchmark 10-year bond yield slipped to 3.828%, driving broad sectoral gains. Materials sector (.GSPTTMT) , including metal miners, gained 3.3% as precious metal prices rebounded on a softer dollar. The S&P 500 ended higher, springing back from early losses as investors concerned about AI stocks shifted into Eli Lilly, UnitedHealth and other healthcare and consumer stocks. Canadian tech equities (.SPTTTK) gained 2.3%, with e-commerce platform Shopify (SHOP.TO) gaining 2.9%. Energy sector (.SPTTEN) slipped 0.5% as investors weighed possible US steps to ease restrictions on the world’s "shadow fleet" of tankers, while conflict in the Middle East kept a geopolitical risk premium in the market. Canadian [USN:AQN2MO654 TEXT:"factory sales"] grew 1.5% in August from July on higher sales of primary metals, data showed on Thursday. Still, economists remain cautious about recovery in manufacturing considering limited sectoral gains. "This reinforces our view that the Bank of Canada will deliver only two of the roughly four rate hikes currently priced in by markets, with tightening serving more as a risk-management exercise against upside inflation risks," said Thomas Ryan, senior North America economist, Capital Economics.

item.title: ‘Whalefall’ film dives deep into father-son bonds within a whale tale
item.description: For Austin Abrams, Disney's 20th Century Studios survival film "Whalefall" is about more than just a young man being trapped inside an enormous sperm whale.
item.dc:creator: Danielle Broadway
item.content:encoded: For Austin Abrams, Disney's (DIS.N) 20th Century Studios survival film "Whalefall" is about more than just a young man being trapped inside an enormous sperm whale. "I feel like what... drew interest for me was this insane story about getting swallowed by a whale," the "Euphoria" actor told Reuters. However, what kept Abrams' attention was the complex father-son relationship at the heart of the story. "Whalefall," which arrives in theaters on Friday, follows Jay Gardiner, played by Abrams, a young man who dives off California's Central Coast in search of his father's remains, only to be swallowed by a massive sperm whale. With just one hour of oxygen left, Jay realizes that the stern lessons his father taught him about the ocean and diving may be his only chance of survival. The film, directed by Brian Duffield, who co-wrote the screenplay with Daniel Kraus, is based on Kraus' novel of the same name. Abrams stars alongside Josh Brolin, who plays Jay's father, Mitt Gardiner. "There's not a dearth of love that the father has for the son or that the son has for the father," Brolin said. "It's just where they're meeting in their lives." Through a series of flashbacks, the film explores the turbulent bond between Jay and Mitt, revealing how Mitt’s relentless drive to make his son share his obsession with the ocean helped fuel their complex relationship. Kraus said the idea for "Whalefall" came from a viral video of a humpback whale surfacing near a kayaker, who briefly ended up in the whale's mouth. His research led him to sperm whales, whose throats are large enough to swallow prey such as giant squid or, in the case of his novel, a person. "So that was the inspiration for the plot," Kraus added, noting that the film truly came together when he decided to center it on a parent-child dynamic.
